claims.statement: In several Bantu mythologies the mokele-mbembe is known.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa mitologi Bantu dikenal mokele-mbembe.
claims.quote: In several Bantu mythologies, mokele-mbembe

claims.statement: Mokele-mbembe is a mythical water-dwelling cryptid believed to exist in the Congo River Basin, variously described as a reptilian creature, a spirit, or a member of the extinct lineage of sauropods.
claims.statement_id: Mokele-mbembe adalah kriptid mitos penghuni air yang dipercaya ada di Lembah Sungai Kongo, digambarkan beragam sebagai makhluk reptil, roh, atau anggota garis keturunan sauropoda yang punah.
claims.quote: is a mythical water-dwelling cryptid that is believed to exist in the Congo River Basin. It is variously described as a reptilian creature, a spirit, or a member of the extinct lineage of sauropods.

claims.statement: In the quoted report, the animal is said to be brownish-gray with smooth skin and about the size of an elephant, at least that of a hippopotamus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam laporan yang dikutip, hewan itu dikatakan berwarna abu-abu kecokelatan, berkulit halus, dan berukuran kira-kira sebesar gajah, setidaknya sebesar kuda nil.
claims.quote: The animal is said to be of a brownish-gray color with a smooth skin, its size is approximately that of an elephant; at least that of a hippopotamus.

claims.statement: Canoes that come near it are said to be doomed; it is said to attack the vessels at once and kill the crews without eating the bodies.
claims.statement_id: Perahu yang mendekatinya dikatakan celaka; hewan itu disebut langsung menyerang perahu dan membunuh awaknya tanpa memakan jasadnya.
claims.quote: Canoes coming near it are said to be doomed; the animal is said to attack the vessels at once and to kill the crews but without eating the bodies.

claims.statement: The creature is said to live in caves washed out by the river in the clay of its shores at sharp bends.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu dikatakan tinggal di gua-gua yang terkikis sungai pada tanah liat tepiannya di tikungan tajam.
claims.quote: The creature is said to live in the caves that have been washed out by the river in the clay of its shores at sharp bends.

claims.statement: Its diet is said to be entirely vegetable.
claims.statement_id: Makanannya dikatakan sepenuhnya nabati.
claims.quote: its diet is said to be entirely vegetable.

claims.statement: The first report of the mokele-mbembe comes from German Captain Ludwig Freiherr von Stein zu Lausnitz.
claims.statement_id: Laporan pertama tentang mokele-mbembe berasal dari Kapten Jerman Ludwig Freiherr von Stein zu Lausnitz.
claims.quote: The first report of the mokele-mbembe comes from German Captain Ludwig Freiherr von Stein zu Lausnitz

claims.statement: Von Stein was ordered to conduct a survey of German colonies in what is now Cameroon in 1913.
claims.statement_id: Von Stein ditugaskan menyurvei koloni Jerman di wilayah yang kini bernama Kamerun pada 1913.
claims.quote: Von Stein was ordered to conduct a survey of German colonies in what is now Cameroon in 1913.

claims.statement: As cited, Bölsche wrote that von Stein clearly believed the creature was not an actual animal but only local folklore.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Bölsche seperti dikutip, von Stein jelas yakin bahwa makhluk itu bukan hewan sungguhan, melainkan hanya cerita rakyat setempat.
claims.quote: von Stein clearly believed that the creature described was not an actual animal, but instead was nothing more than local folklore.

claims.statement: Most mainstream experts believe the mokele-mbembe reported by Congolese natives was probably inspired by the black rhinoceros, which once thrived in the region.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar pakar arus utama meyakini bahwa mokele-mbembe seperti yang dilaporkan penduduk asli Kongo kemungkinan terinspirasi badak hitam yang dahulu berkembang di wilayah itu.
claims.quote: Most mainstream experts believe that mokele-mbembe, as reported by Congolese natives, was probably inspired by the black rhinoceros, which once thrived in the region.

claims.statement: An interview with the Biaka people recorded that they identified the mokele-mbembe as a rhinoceros while looking at an illustrated wildlife manual.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah wawancara dengan orang Biaka mencatat bahwa mereka mengenali mokele-mbembe sebagai badak ketika melihat buku panduan satwa bergambar.
claims.quote: included an interview with the Biaka people who identified the mokele-mbembe as a rhinoceros while looking at an illustrated manual of wildlife.

claims.statement: The lack of physical evidence and the conflicting witnesses have led the large majority of scientists and historians to doubt its existence.
claims.statement_id: Kurangnya bukti fisik dan kesaksian yang saling bertentangan membuat keberadaan makhluk ini diragukan oleh sebagian besar ilmuwan dan sejarawan.
claims.quote: The lack of physical evidence and the conflicting witnesses have made the existence of the entity doubted by the large majority of scientists and historians.

claims.statement: The emela-ntouka, an elephant-sized creature, is said to share many similarities with the mokele-mbembe.
claims.statement_id: Emela-ntouka, makhluk sebesar gajah, disebut memiliki banyak kemiripan dengan mokele-mbembe.
claims.quote: A notable example would be the emela-ntouka, an elephant-sized creature that shares a lot of similarities with the mokele-mbembe.

claims.statement: In the 1985 film Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend, rumors of a mokele-mbembe sighting lead the main characters to a family of live sauropods.
claims.statement_id: Dalam film Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend (1985), kabar penampakan mokele-mbembe membawa para tokoh utama ke sebuah keluarga sauropoda hidup.
claims.quote: In the 1985 film Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend, rumors of a sighting of mokele-mbembe lead the main characters to a family of live sauropods.

claims.statement: The second article calls it the name for a kind of river-dwelling cryptid found in the folk tales and legends of the Congo River Basin.
claims.statement_id: Artikel kedua menyebut mokele-mbembe sebagai nama untuk sejenis kriptid penghuni sungai yang ditemukan dalam cerita dan legenda rakyat Lembah Sungai Kongo.
claims.quote: adalah nama yang diberikan untuk sejenis kriptid yang mendiami sungai, yang ditemukan dalam cerita rakyat dan legenda rakyat yang tinggal di Lembah Sungai Kongo.

claims.statement: The name means "something that holds back the flow of rivers" in Lingala (dalam Bahasa Lingala).
claims.statement_id: Nama itu berarti "sesuatu yang menahan aliran sungai" dalam bahasa Lingala (dalam Bahasa Lingala).
claims.quote: sesuatu yang menahan aliran sungai ... dalam Bahasa Lingala

claims.statement: In the folk tradition of the Congo basin, the mokele-mbembe is known as a plant-eating creature as large as an elephant or hippopotamus (gajah atau kuda nil).
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi rakyat di lembah Sungai Kongo, mokele-mbembe dikenal sebagai makhluk pemakan tanaman sebesar gajah atau kuda nil (gajah atau kuda nil).
claims.quote: Berdasarkan tradisi rakyat di lembah Sungai Kongo, Mokele-mbembe diketahui sebagai mahkluk pemakan tanaman dengan ukuran sebesar gajah atau kuda nil.

claims.statement: It lives in the Congo River and the swampy areas around it (rawa-rawa).
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di Sungai Kongo dan wilayah rawa di sekitarnya (rawa-rawa).
claims.quote: Ia tinggal di Sungai Kongo dan wilayah rawa-rawa di sekitarnya

claims.statement: Some legends describe an elephant-like body with a long neck, a tail and a small head, grey-brown in colour (coklat abu-abu).
claims.statement_id: Beberapa legenda menyebutnya bertubuh seperti gajah dengan leher panjang, ekor panjang, dan kepala kecil, berwarna cokelat keabu-abuan (coklat abu-abu).
claims.quote: Beberapa legenda menyebutkannya memiliki tubuh seperti gajah dengan leher panjang, ekor dan kepala kecil, berwarna coklat abu-abu

claims.statement: The people of the village of Boha regard it more as an incorporeal being than as a living animal (mahkluk tak berwujud).
claims.statement_id: Masyarakat desa Boha lebih menganggapnya makhluk tak berwujud daripada makhluk hidup (mahkluk tak berwujud).
claims.quote: Masyarakat dari desa Boha, lebih menganggapnya sebagai mahkluk tak berwujud daripada mahkluk hidup.

claims.statement: Yemọja (also Yemaja, Yemanjá, Yemoyá, Yemayá) is a major water deity in the Yoruba religion.
claims.statement_id: Yemọja (juga Yemaja, Yemanjá, Yemoyá, Yemayá) adalah dewi air utama dalam agama Yoruba.
claims.quote: Yemọja (also: Yemaja, Yemanjá, Yemoyá, Yemayá; there are many different transliterations in other languages) is a major water deity in the Yoruba religion.

claims.statement: She is an oriṣa and patron spirit of rivers, especially the Ogun River in Nigeria, and of oceans in Cuban and Brazilian Orisha religions.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah seorang oriṣa, roh pelindung sungai, terutama Sungai Ogun di Nigeria, dan roh pelindung samudra dalam agama Orisha di Kuba (Cuban) dan Brasil (Brazilian).
claims.quote: She is an oriṣa, and the patron spirit of rivers, particularly the Ogun River in Nigeria, and of oceans in Cuban and Brazilian Orisha religions.

claims.statement: She is often syncretized with Our Lady of Regla in the Afro-Cuban diaspora or other Virgin Mary figures of the Catholic Church, a practice that emerged in the era of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering disinkretiskan dengan Our Lady of Regla dalam diaspora Afro-Kuba atau dengan figur Perawan Maria (Virgin Mary) lain dari Gereja Katolik, praktik yang muncul pada masa perdagangan budak Trans-Atlantik.
claims.quote: She is often syncretized with either Our Lady of Regla in the Afro-Cuban diaspora or various other Virgin Mary figures of the Catholic Church, a practice that emerged during the era of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade.

claims.statement: Yemọja is said to be motherly and strongly protective, caring deeply for all her children, comforting them and cleansing them of sorrow.
claims.statement_id: Yemọja dikatakan bersifat keibuan dan sangat melindungi, sangat peduli pada semua anaknya, menghibur mereka dan membersihkan mereka dari duka.
claims.quote: Yemọja is said to be motherly and strongly protective, and to care deeply for all her children, comforting them and cleansing them of sorrow.

claims.statement: She does not easily lose her temper, but when angered she can be destructive and violent, like the flood waters of turbulent rivers.
claims.statement_id: Ia tidak mudah marah, tetapi bila marah ia bisa sangat merusak dan keras, seperti air bah sungai yang bergolak.
claims.quote: She does not easily lose her temper, but when angered she can be quite destructive and violent, as the flood waters of turbulent rivers.

claims.statement: Some priests of Yemọja believe she used her fresh water to help Ọbàtálá mould human beings out of clay.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian pendeta Yemọja percaya bahwa ia memakai air tawarnya untuk membantu Ọbàtálá membentuk manusia dari tanah liat.
claims.quote: Some of the priests of Yemọja believe that she used her fresh water to help Ọbàtálá in the molding of human beings out of clay.

claims.statement: Yemọja is often depicted as a mermaid by devotees and, in some diaspora communities, is associated with water, feminine mysteries and the moon.
claims.statement_id: Yemọja sering digambarkan sebagai putri duyung (mermaid) oleh sejumlah pemuja, dan di beberapa komunitas diaspora dikaitkan dengan air, misteri feminin, dan bulan.
claims.quote: Yemọja is often depicted as a mermaid by a number of devotees, and is associated with water, feminine mysteries, and the moon in some diaspora communities.

claims.statement: She is said to be able to cure infertility in women, and cowrie shells represent her wealth.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan mampu menyembuhkan kemandulan pada perempuan, dan cangkang kauri (cowrie) melambangkan kekayaannya.
claims.quote: She is said to be able to cure infertility in women, and cowrie shells represent her wealth.

claims.statement: Her name is a contraction of the Yoruba words Iye (ìyá, mother), ọmọ (child) and ẹja (fish).
claims.statement_id: Namanya adalah singkatan kata-kata Yoruba Iye (ìyá, ibu), ọmọ (anak), dan ẹja (ikan).
claims.quote: Her name is a contraction of the Yoruba words Iye, a dialect variant of "ìyá" meaning "mother"; ọmọ, meaning "child"; and ẹja, meaning "fish"

claims.statement: In West Africa Yemọja is worshipped as a high-ranking river deity, but in Brazil and Cuba mainly as a sea or ocean deity.
claims.statement_id: Di Afrika Barat (West Africa) Yemọja dipuja sebagai dewi sungai berkedudukan tinggi, tetapi di Brasil (Brazil) dan Kuba (Cuba) ia terutama dipuja sebagai dewi laut.
claims.quote: In West Africa, Yemọja is worshipped as a high-ranking river deity, but in Brazil and Cuba she is worshipped mainly as a sea/ocean deity.

claims.statement: In Yorubaland it is Olókun who fills the role of sea deity, while Yemọja leads the other river deities.
claims.statement_id: Di Yorubaland, Olókun yang berperan sebagai dewa laut, sedangkan Yemọja adalah pemimpin para dewi sungai lainnya.
claims.quote: It is Olókun that fills the role of sea deity in Yorubaland, while Yemọja is a leader of the other river deities.

claims.statement: In Candomblé and Umbanda she is the Queen of the Ocean, patron of fishermen and shipwreck survivors, the feminine principle of creation and the spirit of moonlight.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Candomblé dan Umbanda ia adalah Ratu Samudra (Queen of the Ocean), pelindung nelayan dan penyintas kapal karam, prinsip feminin penciptaan, serta roh cahaya bulan.
claims.quote: She is the Queen of the Ocean, the patron spirit of the fishermen and the survivors of shipwrecks, the feminine principle of creation, and the spirit of moonlight.

claims.statement: In Candomblé and Umbanda, Yemanjá is one of the seven Orixás.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Candomblé dan Umbanda, Yemanjá adalah salah satu dari tujuh Orixá.
claims.quote: In Candomblé and Umbanda, Yemanjá is one of the seven Orixás.

claims.statement: Every February 2, thousands of people line up at dawn to leave offerings at her shrine in Rio Vermelho.
claims.statement_id: Setiap 2 Februari (February 2), ribuan orang antre sejak fajar untuk meninggalkan persembahan di tempat sucinya di Rio Vermelho.
claims.quote: Every February 2, thousands of people line up at dawn to leave their offerings at her shrine in Rio Vermelho.

claims.statement: In Santería or regla de ocha, Yemayá is the mother of all living things and the owner of the oceans and seas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Santería atau regla de ocha, Yemayá adalah ibu segala makhluk hidup sekaligus pemilik samudra dan lautan.
claims.quote: In Santería or regla de ocha, Yemayá is the mother of all living things as well as the owner of the oceans and seas.

claims.statement: She is often shown as a water woman (Wasserfrau); in Brazil (Brasilien) she represents the salt water of the sea, while in Nigeria she is a river goddess in Ogun State.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan air (Wasserfrau); di Brasil (Brasilien) ia mewakili air asin laut, sedangkan di Nigeria ia adalah dewi sungai di negara bagian Ogun.
claims.quote: Sie wird daher häufig als Wasserfrau dargestellt und repräsentiert z. B. in Brasilien das Salzwasser des Meeres, in Nigeria ist sie eine Flussgöttin im Bundesstaat Ogun.

claims.statement: In legend Yemayá is married (verheiratet) to Oxalá; because she talked so much he went mad, and Yemayá had to heal him, thereby becoming guardian of heads (Hüterin der Köpfe).
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Yemayá menikah (verheiratet) dengan Oxalá; karena ia terlalu banyak bicara, suaminya menjadi gila, lalu Yemayá harus menyembuhkannya dan dengan itu menjadi penjaga kepala (Hüterin der Köpfe).
claims.quote: Yemayá ist verheiratet mit Oxalá. Da sie so viel mit ihrem Mann redete, wurde er verrückt. ... Yemayá musste ihn heilen und wurde so zur Hüterin der Köpfe.

claims.statement: Her attributes are fish (Fische) and a hand mirror called Abebê; her weekday is Saturday (Samstag).
claims.statement_id: Atributnya adalah ikan (Fische) dan cermin tangan bernama Abebê; hari sucinya adalah Sabtu (Samstag).
claims.quote: Ihre Attribute sind Fische und ein Handspiegel namens Abebê. Ihr Wochentag ist der Samstag.

claims.statement: Yemayá is regarded as one of the most important orishas (wichtigsten Orishas) in Cuba.
claims.statement_id: Yemayá dianggap salah satu orisha terpenting (wichtigsten Orishas) di Kuba.
claims.quote: Yemayá gilt als eine der wichtigsten Orishas auf Kuba.

claims.statement: The third article says many stories tell how she became mother of all spirits (mère de tous les esprits), and states she was married (mariée) to Aganju.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ketiga menyebut banyak kisah tentang bagaimana ia menjadi ibu semua roh (mère de tous les esprits), dan menyatakan ia menikah (mariée) dengan Aganju.
claims.quote: Il existe de nombreuses histoires contant la façon dont elle est devenue la mère de tous les esprits. Elle était mariée à Aganju

claims.statement: Other stories (D'autres histoires) say Yemaya has always existed and all life, including all the orishas, was born from her.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lain (D'autres histoires) menyebut Yemaya selalu ada dan semua kehidupan lahir darinya, termasuk semua orisha.
claims.quote: D'autres histoires racontent que Yemaya a toujours existé et que toute vie est née d'elle, y compris tous les orishas.

claims.statement: Oshun (also Ọṣun, Ochún, Oxúm) is the orisha of the Yoruba religion associated with love, sexuality, fertility, femininity, water, destiny, divination, purity, wealth, prosperity, beauty and the Osun River.
claims.statement_id: Oshun (juga Ọṣun, Ochún, Oxúm) adalah orisha dalam agama Yoruba yang dikaitkan dengan cinta, seksualitas, kesuburan, femininitas, air, takdir, ramalan, kemurnian, kekayaan, kemakmuran, kecantikan, dan Sungai Osun.
claims.quote: Oshun (also Ọṣun, Ochún, and Oxúm) is the orisha associated with love, sexuality, fertility, femininity, water, destiny, divination, purity, wealth, prosperity and beauty, and the Osun River, in the Yoruba religion.

claims.statement: She is considered one of the most popular and venerated of the 401 orishas.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap salah satu yang paling populer dan dihormati di antara 401 orisha.
claims.quote: She is considered one of the most popular and venerated of the 401 orishas.

claims.statement: According to traditional beliefs, Oshun was once queen consort to King Shango of Oyo and was deified after her death; she is honoured at the Osun-Osogbo Festival, a two-week annual festival usually held in August at the Oṣun-Osogbo Sacred Grove in Osogbo.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan tradisional, Oshun dahulu permaisuri Raja Shango dari Oyo dan didewakan setelah wafat; ia dihormati dalam Festival Osun-Osogbo, festival tahunan dua minggu yang biasanya berlangsung pada Agustus (August) di Hutan Suci Oṣun-Osogbo (Sacred Grove) di Osogbo.
claims.quote: According to traditional beliefs, Oshun was once the queen consort to King Shango of Oyo, and deified following her death, honored at the Osun-Osogbo Festival, a two-week-long annual festival that usually takes place in August, at the Oṣun-Osogbo Sacred Grove in Osogbo.

claims.statement: According to the Ifa Literary Corpus, Oshun was the only female Irunmole (primordial spirit) sent by Olodumare, the Supreme God, to help Shango create the world.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ifa Literary Corpus, Oshun adalah satu-satunya Irunmole (roh primordial) perempuan yang diutus Olodumare, Tuhan Tertinggi (Supreme God), untuk membantu Shango menciptakan dunia.
claims.quote: According to the Ifa Literary Corpus, Oshun was the only female Irunmole (primordial spirit) sent to assist Shango to create the world by Olodumare, the Supreme God.

claims.statement: One version claims the female spirits acted on their own, but all their creative attempts failed because they acted without male spiritual leadership.
claims.statement_id: Satu versi menyebut roh-roh perempuan bertindak sendiri, tetapi semua upaya penciptaan mereka gagal karena bertindak tanpa kepemimpinan spiritual laki-laki.
claims.quote: One version of the story claims that female spirits were tempted to take matters into their own hands, but all of their creative attempts failed because they acted without male spiritual leadership.

claims.statement: Another version claims the male spirits tried to make the world without female influence, and this exclusion caused the world to fail.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain menyebut roh-roh laki-laki mencoba membuat dunia tanpa pengaruh perempuan, dan pengucilan itulah yang membuat dunia gagal.
claims.quote: Another version, one more consistent with the beginning of the story, claims that the male spirits attempted to make the world without female influence, and this exclusion is what caused the world to fail.

claims.statement: Whatever the version, the myth ends with Shango forcing the other spirits to respect Oshun as they would him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi mana pun, mitos itu berakhir dengan Shango memaksa roh-roh lain menghormati Oshun seperti mereka menghormatinya.
claims.quote: Regardless of the version, the myth ends with Shango forcing the other spirits to respect Oshun as they would him.

claims.statement: Oshun is the divine patroness of the Osun River in Nigeria, which bears her name.
claims.statement_id: Oshun adalah pelindung ilahi Sungai Osun di Nigeria, yang menyandang namanya.
claims.quote: Oshun is the divine patroness of the Osun River in Nigeria, which bears her name.

claims.statement: Ọshun was adopted into Afro-Brazilian religions, keeping her role as goddess of love, beauty and waters, with added power over wealth and prosperity.
claims.statement_id: Ọshun diadopsi ke dalam agama-agama Afro-Brasil (Afro-Brazilian), tetap sebagai dewi cinta, kecantikan, dan perairan, dengan tambahan kuasa atas kekayaan dan kemakmuran.
claims.quote: Ọshun was adopted into Afro-Brazilian religions, retaining her role as the goddess of love, beauty, and waters, with the addition of power over wealth and prosperity.

claims.statement: Oshun is worshipped at rivers and waterfalls, more rarely near mineral springs; she is a symbol of sensitivity and is identified by weeping.
claims.statement_id: Oshun dipuja di sungai dan air terjun, dan lebih jarang di dekat sumber air mineral; ia lambang kepekaan dan dikenali lewat tangisan.
claims.quote: Oshun is worshiped at rivers and waterfalls, and more rarely, near mineral water sources. She is a symbol of sensitivity and is identified by weeping.

claims.statement: In Candomblé Ketu, Oshun is the deity of fresh water and patron of gestation and fecundity, receiving the prayers of women who wish for children and protecting them during pregnancy.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Candomblé Ketu, Oshun adalah dewi air tawar dan pelindung kehamilan serta kesuburan, yang menerima doa perempuan yang ingin punya anak dan melindungi mereka selama hamil.
claims.quote: In Candomblé Ketu, Oshun is the deity of fresh water; the patron of gestation and fecundity; and receives the prayers of women who wish to have children and protect them during pregnancy.

claims.statement: Ochún is syncretized with Our Lady of Charity, while Ozun is a distinct masculine Orisha associated with John the Baptist.
claims.statement_id: Ochún disinkretiskan dengan Our Lady of Charity, sedangkan Ozun adalah Orisha maskulin berbeda yang dikaitkan dengan John the Baptist.
claims.quote: While Ozun is a masculine Orisha associated with John the Baptist, Ochún is syncretized with Our Lady of Charity.

claims.statement: She is the river goddess (Flussgöttin) of the river of the same name in Nigeria and symbolises fertility (Fruchtbarkeit).
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah dewi sungai (Flussgöttin) dari sungai bernama sama di Nigeria dan melambangkan kesuburan (Fruchtbarkeit).
claims.quote: Sie ist eine Flussgöttin des gleichnamigen Flusses Oshun in Nigeria und symbolisiert die Fruchtbarkeit.

claims.statement: Her grove (Hain) in Oshogbo is a UNESCO World Heritage site (UNESCO-Welterbe).
claims.statement_id: Hutan sucinya (Hain) di Oshogbo termasuk Warisan Dunia UNESCO (UNESCO-Welterbe).
claims.quote: Ihr Hain in Oshogbo (Oṣogbo) gehört zum UNESCO-Welterbe.

claims.statement: Depending on the legend (je nach Legende), Oxum is the daughter of Oxalá, sister of Obá, married to Xangô, Oxóssi and Ogum, and has a son, Logum Edé.
claims.statement_id: Menurut berbagai legenda (je nach Legende), Oxum adalah putri Oxalá, saudari Obá, menikah dengan Xangô, Oxóssi, dan Ogum, dan memiliki seorang putra, Logum Edé.
claims.quote: Oxum ist – je nach Legende unterschiedlich erzählt – die Tochter von Oxalá, die Schwester von Obá, verheiratet mit Xangô, Oxóssi und Ogum und hat einen Sohn, Logum Edé.

claims.statement: Because her element is gold (Gold), she wears yellow (Gelb).
claims.statement_id: Karena unsurnya adalah emas (Gold), ia mengenakan warna kuning (Gelb).
claims.quote: Da ihr Element das Gold ist, trägt sie Gelb.

claims.statement: In Afro-Cuban (afro-kubanischen) Santería, Oshun corresponds to the Virgin Mary (Jungfrau Maria) as the Virgin of Charity of Cobre, patroness of Cuba (Kubas).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Santería Afro-Kuba (afro-kubanischen), Oshun dipadankan dengan Perawan Maria (Jungfrau Maria) dalam wujud Perawan Belas Kasih dari Cobre, pelindung Kuba (Kubas).
claims.quote: In der afro-kubanischen Santería entspricht Oshun der Jungfrau Maria in Form der Barmherzigen Jungfrau von Cobre, der Schutzpatronin Kubas.

claims.statement: In one legend Oxum refused her exclusion (Ausschluss), took revenge on the male Orixás and condemned all women to infertility (Unfruchtbarkeit).
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu legenda, Oxum menolak dikucilkan (Ausschluss), membalas para Orixá laki-laki, dan mengutuk semua perempuan menjadi mandul (Unfruchtbarkeit).
claims.quote: Oxum nahm diese Situation nicht hin. Sie lehnte sich gegen den Ausschluss auf, sie rächte sich an den männlichen Orixás. Sie verdammte alle Frauen zur Unfruchtbarkeit.

claims.statement: Oxum always appears accompanied (Begleitung) by Yemayá and is especially a help to pregnant women and those giving birth (Schwangere und Gebärende).
claims.statement_id: Oxum selalu muncul bersama (Begleitung) Yemayá dan terutama menolong perempuan hamil dan yang melahirkan (Schwangere und Gebärende).
claims.quote: Oxum tritt stets in Begleitung von Yemayá auf und ist im Besonderen eine Hilfe für Schwangere und Gebärende.

claims.statement: Mami Wata is a mermaid, water spirit and/or goddess in the folklore of parts of Western, Central, Eastern and Southern Africa.
claims.statement_id: Mami Wata adalah putri duyung, roh air, dan/atau dewi dalam cerita rakyat sebagian Afrika Barat, Afrika Tengah, Afrika Timur, dan Afrika Selatan (Western, Central, Eastern, Southern Africa).
claims.quote: is a mermaid, water spirit, and/or goddess in the folklore of parts of Western Africa, Central Africa, Eastern Africa, and Southern Africa.

claims.statement: Scholars trace her origins to early encounters between Europeans and West Africans in the 15th century, when Mami Wata developed from depictions of European mermaids.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana menelusuri asal-usulnya ke perjumpaan awal orang Eropa (Europeans) dan Afrika Barat pada abad ke-15, ketika Mami Wata berkembang dari gambaran putri duyung Eropa.
claims.quote: Historically, scholars trace her origins to early encounters between Europeans and West Africans in the 15th century, where Mami Wata developed from depictions of European mermaids.

claims.statement: She is often depicted as a fair-skinned woman with long flowing hair, interested in foreign objects that her adherents place at her shrines.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan berkulit terang dengan rambut panjang tergerai, yang menyukai benda-benda asing yang diletakkan pemujanya di tempat suci (shrines).
claims.quote: often depicted as a fair-skinned woman with long, flowing hair and a particular interest in objects foreign to West Africans that her adherents place at her shrines.

claims.statement: In the mid-19th century, Mami Wata's iconography was strongly influenced by an image of the snake charmer Nala Damajanti spreading from Europe.
claims.statement_id: Pada pertengahan abad ke-19, ikonografi Mami Wata sangat dipengaruhi gambar pawang ular Nala Damajanti yang menyebar dari Eropa (Europe).
claims.quote: In the mid-19th century, Mami Wata's iconography became particularly influenced by an image of snake charmer Nala Damajanti spreading from Europe.

claims.statement: Mami is a goddess of wealth, fertility, healing, wisdom and beauty; she can manipulate oceans and rivers and can transform to seduce and mesmerize humans.
claims.statement_id: Mami adalah dewi kekayaan, kesuburan, penyembuhan, kebijaksanaan, dan kecantikan; ia berkuasa mengendalikan samudra dan sungai serta mampu berubah wujud untuk merayu dan memukau manusia.
claims.quote: Mami is a goddess of wealth, fertility, healing, wisdom, and profound beauty. She holds the power to manipulate the oceans and rivers, and possesses the ability to transform in order to seduce and mesmerize humans with her alluring beauty.

claims.statement: Mami Wata is venerated in parts of Africa and the Atlantic diaspora, and has been demonized in some African Christian and Islamic communities.
claims.statement_id: Mami Wata terutama dipuja di sebagian Afrika (Africa) dan diaspora Atlantik, tetapi juga dijadikan setan oleh sebagian komunitas Kristen dan Islam (Christian, Islamic) di wilayah itu.
claims.quote: Mami Wata is especially venerated in parts of Africa and in the Atlantic diaspora and has also been demonized in some African Christian and Islamic communities in the region.

claims.statement: The names Mami Wata, Mami Wota or Mammy Wata derive from the English nouns mother and water in several English-based creole languages in Africa, including Krio and Naijá.
claims.statement_id: Nama Mami Wata, Mami Wota, atau Mammy Wata berasal dari kata benda bahasa Inggris (English) mother (ibu) dan water (air) dalam beberapa bahasa kreol di Afrika, termasuk Krio dan Naijá.
claims.quote: The names Mami Wata, Mami Wota, or Mammy Wata derive from the English language nouns mother and water in multiple English-based creole languages in Africa, including Krio and Naijá.

claims.statement: Mamba Muntu, Mami Muntu or Dona Fish is the Central African variant of the water spirit, found in Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo.
claims.statement_id: Mamba Muntu, Mami Muntu, atau Dona Fish adalah varian Afrika Tengah dari roh air ini yang ada di Angola, Republik Demokratik Kongo (Congo), dan Republik Kongo.
claims.quote: Mamba Muntu, Mami Muntu, or Dona Fish is the Central African variant of the water spirit that exists in Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo.

claims.statement: This variant has been identified as a mermaid, a crocodile and a snake.
claims.statement_id: Varian ini diidentifikasi sebagai putri duyung, buaya, dan ular.
claims.quote: She has been identified as a mermaid, a crocodile, and a snake.

claims.statement: Some scholars posit that Mami Wata is related to similar water spirits in the Caribbean and South America, including Lasirèn.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sarjana berpendapat Mami Wata berkerabat dengan roh air serupa di Karibia (Caribbean) dan Amerika Selatan (South America), termasuk Lasirèn.
claims.quote: Some scholars have posited that Mami Wata is related to similar water spirits found in the Caribbean and South America, including Lasirèn

claims.statement: People in Liberia believe she lives in a mansion under the water and sometimes comes ashore to comb her long hair with a golden comb.
claims.statement_id: Di Liberia orang percaya ia tinggal di istana di bawah air dan kadang naik ke pantai untuk menyisir rambut panjangnya dengan sisir emas (golden comb).
claims.quote: People believe that she lives in a mansion under the water, from which she some times ventures on to the shore to comb out her long hair with a golden comb.

claims.statement: Mammy Water may also gift extra-sensory perception, including foresight and seeing what others cannot, or especially swift travels.
claims.statement_id: Mammy Water juga dapat menganugerahkan persepsi ekstrasensori, termasuk melihat masa depan dan melihat yang tak terlihat orang lain, atau perjalanan yang sangat cepat.
claims.quote: Mammy Water may also gift extra-sensory perception, including foresight and the ability to see that which others cannot, or especially swift travels.

claims.statement: If a favoured man is unfaithful, it is said Mami Wata will strip him of his wealth and make him fall ill or become insane.
claims.statement_id: Bila lelaki yang diberkatinya tidak setia, Mami Wata dikatakan akan mencabut kekayaannya dan membuatnya sakit atau gila.
claims.quote: it is said Mami Wata will strip the man of his wealth, as well as make them fall ill or become insane.

claims.statement: Mirrors are a symbol of Mami Wata, used in her shrines to draw her attention to her devotees.
claims.statement_id: Cermin (mirrors) dianggap lambang Mami Wata dan dipakai di tempat sucinya untuk menarik perhatiannya kepada para pemuja.
claims.quote: Mirrors are seen as a symbol for Mami Wata, primarily used within shrines dedicated to her as a way to get her attention towards her devotees.

claims.statement: A secondary development in some traditions is Papi Wata, a male entity associated with Mami Wata.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian tradisi berkembang Papi Wata, sosok laki-laki yang dikaitkan dengan Mami Wata.
claims.quote: A secondary development of Mami Wata in some traditions is Papi Wata, a male entity associated with Mami Wata.

claims.statement: The second source describes Mami Wata as water spirit, mermaid and serpent, decidedly female, present across many eras, cultures and continents with shifting meaning.
claims.statement_id: Sumber kedua menggambarkan Mami Wata sebagai roh air, putri duyung, dan ular yang tegas perempuan, yang hadir di banyak zaman, budaya, dan benua dengan makna yang bergeser.
claims.quote: Water spirit, mermaid, serpent, decidedly and decisively female, Mami Wata twines herself through many eras, cultures, and continents, with attendant shifts in meaning and importance.

claims.statement: The possible origin of Mami lies in the first African-European encounters along the African coast, with variations in imagery and meaning added over the centuries.
claims.statement_id: Kemungkinan asal Mami terletak pada perjumpaan pertama Afrika-Eropa (African-European) di pesisir Afrika, dengan variasi citra dan makna yang ditambahkan selama berabad-abad.
claims.quote: the possible origin of Mami lies in the first African-European encounters along the African coast, with variations in imagery and meaning added over the centuries through many other stimuli, both external and internal to Africa.

claims.statement: Mami Wata was introduced by African slaves and later identified in Brazil as Yemanja.
claims.statement_id: Mami Wata dibawa oleh budak Afrika (African slaves) dan kemudian di Brasil (Brazil) diidentikkan dengan Yemanja.
claims.quote: From the introduction of Mami Wata by African slaves, through her subsequent identity in Brazil as Yemanja

claims.statement: The third article calls Mami Wata (Pidgin English for mother of the water, Mutter des Wassers), also Mammy Water, an African water goddess (Wassergöttin) worshipped by the Fon and Ewe and in Haitian (Haitianischen) Voodoo.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ketiga menyebut Mami Wata (Pidgin-Englisch untuk ibu air, Mutter des Wassers), juga Mammy Water, dewi air Afrika (Wassergöttin) yang dipuja orang Fon dan Ewe serta dalam Voodoo Haiti (Haitianischen).
claims.quote: Mami Wata (Pidgin-Englisch für „Mutter des Wassers“), auch Mammy Water, ist eine afrikanische Wassergöttin, die von den Fon und Ewe sowie im Haitianischen Voodoo verehrt wird.

claims.statement: The ethnologist Barbara Paxson instead places Mami Wata's homeland in Latin America (Lateinamerika).
claims.statement_id: Etnolog Barbara Paxson justru menempatkan asal Mami Wata di Amerika Latin (Lateinamerika).
claims.quote: Die Ethnologin Barbara Paxson lokalisiert die Heimat Mami Watas hingegen in Lateinamerika.

claims.statement: Among the Liberian (liberianischen) Kpelle, Mami Wata is sometimes a male (männlich), sometimes a female (weiblich) spirit.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Kpelle di Liberia (liberianischen), Mami Wata kadang roh berwujud laki-laki (männlich), kadang perempuan (weiblich).
claims.quote: Bei den liberianischen Kpelle dagegen ist Mami Wata mal ein männlich, mal ein weiblich geformter Geist.

claims.statement: Like the element of water, the spirit has an ambivalent character (ambivalenter Charakter): healing and life-giving, but also destructive and harmful.
claims.statement_id: Seperti unsur air, roh ini berwatak ambivalen (ambivalenter Charakter): menyembuhkan dan memberi hidup, tetapi juga merusak dan merugikan.
claims.quote: Für den Geist ist ähnlich wie für das Element Wasser ein ambivalenter Charakter kennzeichnend, der sowohl heilende und lebenspendende, aber auch zerstörerische und schädliche Aspekte beinhaltet.

claims.statement: Madam Koi Koi (also called Lady Koi Koi, and Madam Moke in Ghana) is a Nigerian urban legend of a vengeful ghost believed to haunt dormitories, hallways and toilets in boarding schools at night.
claims.statement_id: Madam Koi Koi (juga disebut Lady Koi Koi, dan Madam Moke di Ghana) adalah legenda urban Nigeria tentang hantu pendendam yang dipercaya menghantui asrama, lorong, dan toilet sekolah berasrama pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Madam Koi Koi (also known as Lady Koi Koi and Madam Moke in Ghana) is a Nigerian urban legend of a vengeful ghost who is believed to haunt dormitories, hallways and toilets in boarding schools at night

claims.statement: In day schools she haunts toilets and students who come to school too early or leave too late.
claims.statement_id: Di sekolah harian, ia menghantui toilet dan para murid yang datang ke sekolah terlalu pagi atau pulang terlalu sore.
claims.quote: in day schools, she haunts toilets and students who come to school too early or leave school late.

claims.statement: She is often depicted wearing a pair of red heels or only a single heel.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering digambarkan memakai sepasang sepatu hak merah atau hanya sebelah sepatu hak.
claims.quote: She is often depicted wearing a pair of red heels or wearing a single heel.

claims.statement: The name is taken from the sound her heels make whenever she comes to prey on students at night.
claims.statement_id: Nama itu diambil dari bunyi hak sepatunya setiap kali ia datang mengincar murid pada malam hari.
claims.quote: is taken from the sound her heels make whenever she comes to prey on students at night.

claims.statement: In one version she was dismissed after slapping a female student and damaging her ear, died in an accident on the way home, and before dying swore to take revenge on the school and its students.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi, ia dipecat setelah menampar murid perempuan hingga telinganya rusak, lalu tewas dalam kecelakaan di perjalanan pulang dan sebelum mati bersumpah membalas dendam kepada sekolah dan murid-muridnya.
claims.quote: She was dismissed after slapping a female student and damaging her ear. On her journey back home, she was involved in an accident and died. Before her death, she swore that she would take revenge on the school and its students.

claims.statement: In another version the students cornered her one night as she left the school, gagged her to stop her screaming, and beat her mercilessly until she died.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lain, para murid menyudutkannya saat ia meninggalkan sekolah pada suatu malam, menyumpal mulutnya agar tidak berteriak, dan memukulinya tanpa ampun hingga tewas.
claims.quote: One night, as she was leaving the school, the students cornered her, gagged her to prevent her from screaming, and beat her mercilessly, killing her.

claims.statement: Madam Koi Koi is known mainly for haunting school premises, with activities ranging from opening doors, singing and whistling to attacking people in restrooms or slapping students.
claims.statement_id: Madam Koi Koi terutama dikenal menghantui lingkungan sekolah, dengan tindakan mulai dari membuka pintu, bernyanyi, dan bersiul hingga menyerang orang di toilet atau menampar murid.
claims.quote: Madam Koi Koi is primarily known for haunting school premises with activities that range from opening school doors, singing, and whistling to attacking people in restrooms or slapping students.

claims.statement: She may also be invisible, except for her heel.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dapat tak terlihat, kecuali sepatu haknya.
claims.quote: She may also be invisible, except for her heel.

claims.statement: She is one of the most popular boarding school ghosts in Nigeria.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah salah satu hantu sekolah berasrama yang paling populer di Nigeria.
claims.quote: She is one of the most popular boarding school ghosts in Nigeria.

claims.statement: The second article says it is not known where the legend comes from, but the story of a teacher who roams schools as a ghost in red high heels (roten High Heels) has been told in several versions in Nigeria since the middle of the twentieth century (Mitte des zwanzigsten Jahrhunderts).
claims.statement_id: Artikel kedua menyatakan tidak diketahui dari mana legenda ini berasal, tetapi kisah guru yang menjadi hantu bersepatu hak merah (roten High Heels) diceritakan dalam beberapa versi di Nigeria sejak pertengahan abad kedua puluh (Mitte des zwanzigsten Jahrhunderts).
claims.quote: Es ist nicht bekannt, worauf die Legende zurückgeht, jedoch wird die Geschichte einer Lehrerin, die als Geist mit roten High Heels durch die Schulen zieht, in Nigeria seit Mitte des zwanzigsten Jahrhunderts in mehreren Versionen erzählt.

claims.statement: In the Ghanaian version (ghanaischen Version) she is called Madam Moke, with moke meaning high heels (hohe Absätze).
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Ghana (ghanaischen Version), ia disebut Madam Moke, dengan moke berarti hak tinggi (hohe Absätze).
claims.quote: In der ghanaischen Version der Legende, in der sie Madam Moke genannt wird, wobei Moke übersetzt hohe Absätze bedeutet

claims.statement: Another report says she was struck with one of her red shoes (roten Schuhe) and then left to die.
claims.statement_id: Menurut laporan lain, ia dipukul dengan salah satu sepatu merahnya (roten Schuhe) lalu dibiarkan mati.
claims.quote: Alternativ wird berichtet, sie sei mit einem ihrer roten Schuhe geschlagen und dann zum Sterben liegengelassen worden.

claims.statement: The third article describes a secondary-school teacher (enseignante) known for her beauty who wore red heels (talons rouges).
claims.statement_id: Artikel ketiga menyebut seorang guru sekolah menengah (enseignante) yang terkenal karena kecantikannya mengenakan sepatu hak merah (talons rouges).
claims.quote: Une enseignante dans une école secondaire connue pour sa beauté portait des talons rouges.

claims.statement: The third article calls Madame Koi Koi an urban legend (légende urbaine).
claims.statement_id: Artikel ketiga menyebut Madame Koi Koi sebagai legenda urban (légende urbaine).
claims.quote: Madame Koi Koi est une légende urbaine.

claims.statement: Mawu-Lisa is a creator deity in Gbe mythology and West African Vodun, particularly of the former Dahomey Kingdom (now Benin).
claims.statement_id: Mawu-Lisa adalah dewa pencipta dalam mitologi Gbe dan Vodun Afrika Barat, terutama di bekas Kerajaan Dahomey (kini Benin).
claims.quote: Mawu-Lisa is a creator deity in Gbe mythology and West African Vodun, particularly of the former Dahomey Kingdom (now Benin).

claims.statement: It is a dual deity formed by Mawu (also Mahu, Mau), a goddess associated with the Sun, and Lisa, a god of the Moon; together they are an agender deity.
claims.statement_id: Mawu-Lisa adalah dewa ganda yang dibentuk oleh Mawu (juga Mahu, Mau), dewi yang dikaitkan dengan Matahari (Sun), dan Lisa, dewa Bulan (Moon); bersama-sama mereka dewa tanpa gender.
claims.quote: It is a dual deity, formed by Mawu (alternately: Mahu, Mau), a goddess associated with the Sun, and Lisa, a god of the Moon; put together, they are an agender deity.

claims.statement: Mawu and Lisa are the children of Nana Buluku and the parents of Oba Koso (Shango), known as Hebioso among the Fon.
claims.statement_id: Mawu dan Lisa adalah anak Nana Buluku dan orang tua Oba Koso (Shango), yang dikenal sebagai Hebioso di kalangan Fon.
claims.quote: Mawu and Lisa are the children of Nana Buluku, and are the parents of Oba Koso (Shango), known as Hebioso among the Fon.

claims.statement: According to myth, Mawu alone created human beings from clay, while her husband Lisa was instructed by her to teach humans to build civilization.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos, Mawu satu-satunya pencipta manusia dari tanah liat, sedangkan suaminya Lisa diperintahkannya mengajari manusia membangun peradaban.
claims.quote: According to myth, Mawu is the sole creator of human beings from clay, while her husband Lisa was instructed by her to teach humans how to build civilization.

claims.statement: Mawu worried the earth might be too heavy, so she asked the primeval serpent Aido Hwedo to curl up beneath it and thrust it up into the sky.
claims.statement_id: Mawu khawatir bumi terlalu berat, maka ia meminta ular purba Aido Hwedo melingkar di bawah bumi dan mendorongnya ke langit.
claims.quote: Mawu became concerned that it might be too heavy, so she asked the primeval serpent, Aido Hwedo, to curl up beneath the earth and thrust it up in the sky.

claims.statement: Lisa gave the arrogant monkey Awe a bowl of porridge containing the seed of death and reminded him that only his wife Mawu could give life, and could also take it away.
claims.statement_id: Lisa memberi monyet sombong Awe semangkuk bubur berisi benih kematian dan mengingatkannya bahwa hanya istrinya, Mawu, yang dapat memberi kehidupan dan juga mencabutnya.
claims.quote: Lisa made him a bowl of porridge with the seed of death in it and reminded him that only his wife Mawu could give life, and that she could also take it away.

claims.statement: It became common to use the goddess's name Mawu as the Dahomey equivalent of the One God of Christianity.
claims.statement_id: Lama-kelamaan nama dewi Mawu lazim dipakai sebagai padanan Dahomey untuk Tuhan Yang Esa agama Kristen (Christianity).
claims.quote: it became common to use Mawu, the goddess's name as the Dahomey equivalent of the One God of Christianity.

claims.statement: It became the state deity of Dahomey, but the Mawu-Lisa pair was not originally Fon; they were deities borrowed from Yoruba culture.
claims.statement_id: Mawu-Lisa menjadi dewa negara Dahomey, tetapi pasangan ini semula bukan fenomena Fon melainkan dewa-dewa yang dipinjam dari budaya Yoruba.
claims.quote: It became the state deity of Dahomey, but ultimately, the Mawu-Lisa dyad was not originally a Fon phenomenon, and were deities borrowed from Yoruba culture

claims.statement: The second article says Mawu is the name of the creator deity (divinité créatrice) in the religion of the Ewe (éwé) peoples of Togo and Benin (Bénin), West Africa.
claims.statement_id: Artikel kedua menyebut Mawu nama dewa pencipta (divinité créatrice) dalam agama orang Ewe (éwé) di Togo dan Benin (Bénin), Afrika Barat.
claims.quote: Mawu est l'appellation de la divinité créatrice dans la religion des peuples éwé du Togo et du Bénin, en Afrique de l'Ouest.

claims.statement: In the Ewe language (langue éwé), Mawu means that which cannot be surpassed (ce que l'on ne peut pas dépasser).
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Ewe (langue éwé), Mawu berarti yang tidak dapat dilampaui (ce que l'on ne peut pas dépasser).
claims.quote: Mawu signifie en langue éwé « ce que l'on ne peut pas dépasser ».

claims.statement: According to the second article, Mawu is associated with the Moon (Lune), night, the east and motherhood (maternité).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel kedua, Mawu dikaitkan dengan Bulan (Lune), malam, timur, dan keibuan (maternité).
claims.quote: Elle est associée à la Lune, à la nuit, à l'est et à la maternité.

claims.statement: Among the Fon of Benin (Bénin), Mawu is the daughter of Nana Buluku and the twin sister (sœur jumelle) of Lisa.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Fon di Benin (Bénin), Mawu adalah putri Nana Buluku dan saudari kembar (sœur jumelle) Lisa.
claims.quote: Chez les Fon du Bénin, Mawu est la fille de Nana Buluku, et la sœur jumelle de Lisa.

claims.statement: According to Ellis, the god himself is the indwelling spirit of the firmament, the deified canopy of the heavens.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ellis, dewa ini tidak lain roh yang bersemayam di cakrawala, kubah langit yang didewakan.
claims.quote: the god himself is no other than the indwelling spirit of the firmament, the deified canopy of the heavens.

claims.statement: Ellis writes that the Ewe-speaking peoples regard Mawu as the most powerful of the gods, but not a supreme being or creator.
claims.statement_id: Ellis menulis bahwa orang berbahasa Ewe (Ewe-speaking peoples) menganggap Mawu dewa paling berkuasa, tetapi bukan makhluk tertinggi atau pencipta.
claims.quote: Mawu, then, is regarded by the Ewe-speaking peoples as the most powerful of the gods, but he is not a supreme being or creator.

claims.statement: According to Ellis, sacrifice is never directly offered to him and prayer rarely; he is ignored rather than worshipped.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ellis, korban tidak pernah dipersembahkan langsung kepadanya dan doa jarang; ia lebih diabaikan daripada dipuja.
claims.quote: sacrifice is never directly offered to him, and prayer rarely. He is in fact ignored rather than worshipped.

claims.statement: Mawu controls the rain supply and keeps a vast store of water in the firmament, which he lets out at will.
claims.statement_id: Mawu mengendalikan pasokan hujan dan menyimpan air dalam jumlah besar di cakrawala, yang ia lepaskan sesuka hati.
claims.quote: Mawu controls the rain supply, and keeps a vast store of water in the firmament, which he lets out at will.

claims.statement: According to Ellis, the word Mawu, besides being a proper name, also means sky, firmament and rain, and derives from wu (to stretch over, or overshadow).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ellis, kata Mawu selain nama diri juga berarti langit, cakrawala, dan hujan, dan berasal dari wu (membentang di atas, menaungi).
claims.quote: a word which, besides being a proper name, has also the meanings of sky, firmament, and rain. It is derived from wu (to stretch over, or overshadow)

claims.statement: Ayida Wedo is a powerful loa spirit in Haitian vodou, revered in regions of Africa (including the former Dahomey kingdom/Benin, Togo and southeastern Ghana) and the Caribbean.
claims.statement_id: Ayida Wedo adalah roh loa yang kuat dalam vodou Haiti, dihormati di wilayah Afrika (termasuk bekas Kerajaan Dahomey/Benin, Togo, dan Ghana tenggara) serta Karibia (Caribbean).
claims.quote: is a powerful loa spirit in Haiti vodoo ... revered in regions across Africa (including the former Dahomey kingdom/Benin,Togo and Southeastern Ghana) and the Caribbean, a part of the African diaspora religions.

claims.statement: In a cosmic mythical context the deities are thought to have existed before the Earth, and Ayida Wedo assisted the creator goddess Mawu-Lisa in forming the world.
claims.statement_id: Dalam konteks mitos kosmis, para dewa ini dianggap sudah ada sebelum Bumi, dan Ayida Wedo membantu dewi pencipta Mawu-Lisa membentuk dunia.
claims.quote: In a more cosmic mythical context, the deities are thought to have existed before the Earth, Ayida Wedo assisted the creator goddess Mawu-Lisa in the formation of the world,

claims.statement: In Haitian Vodou, Ayida Wedo is syncretized with the Catholic figure of Our Lady of Immaculate Conception for her association with serpents and rainbow-colored cherubs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Vodou Haiti (Haitian), Ayida Wedo disinkretiskan dengan figur Katolik Our Lady of Immaculate Conception karena kaitannya dengan ular dan kerub berwarna pelangi.
claims.quote: Ayida Wedo is syncretized in Haitian Vodou with the Catholic figure of Our Lady of Immaculate Conception for her association with serpents and rainbow-colored cherubs.

claims.statement: As Mawu-Lisa created the world, the serpent carried the goddess in its mouth while she shaped the Earth with her creations.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Mawu-Lisa menciptakan dunia, ular itu membawa sang dewi di mulutnya selagi ia membentuk Bumi dengan ciptaannya.
claims.quote: As Mawu-Lisa created the world, the serpent carried the goddess in its mouth as she shaped the Earth with her creations.

claims.statement: As they went across the land, the rainbow serpent's body left behind canyons, rivers, valleys and mountains.
claims.statement_id: Ketika mereka melintasi daratan, tubuh ular pelangi meninggalkan ngarai, sungai, lembah, dan gunung.
claims.quote: As they went across the land, the rainbow serpent's body left behind the canyons, rivers, valleys, and mountains.

claims.statement: In Haiti, Ayida Wedo is said to have crossed the ocean with her husband Damballa to carry the knowledge and traditions of Vodou from Africa to the Caribbean.
claims.statement_id: Di Haiti, Ayida Wedo dikatakan menyeberangi samudra bersama suaminya Damballa untuk membawa pengetahuan dan tradisi Vodou dari Afrika ke Karibia.
claims.quote: In Haiti, Ayida Wedo is said to have crossed the ocean with her husband Damballa to take the ancient knowledge and traditions of Vodou from Africa to the Caribbean.

claims.statement: While Damballa slithered under the ocean, Ayida Wedo flew across the sky as the rainbow until the two loa reunited in Haiti, bringing Vodou to the Americas.
claims.statement_id: Sementara Damballa merayap di bawah samudra, Ayida Wedo terbang melintasi langit dalam wujud pelangi sampai keduanya bertemu lagi di Haiti dan membawa Vodou ke Amerika (Americas).
claims.quote: As Damballa slithered under the ocean, Ayida Wedo flew across the sky in the form of the rainbow until the two loa reunited in Haiti, bringing Vodou to the Americas.

claims.statement: During a possession ritual the medium of Ayida Wedo wears white cloth and a jeweled headdress and embodies the serpent by slithering on the ground.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ritual kerasukan, medium Ayida Wedo mengenakan kain putih dan hiasan kepala berpermata, dan memerankan ular dengan merayap di tanah.
claims.quote: The medium of the Ayida Wedo during a spirit possession ritual dons white cloth and a jeweled headdress, and embodies the serpent by slithering upon the ground.

claims.statement: Ayida Wedo is associated with blue and white, the colors of the sky and cloud.
claims.statement_id: Ayida Wedo dikaitkan dengan warna biru dan putih, warna langit dan awan.
claims.quote: Ayida Wedo is associated with blue and white, the colors of the sky and cloud.

claims.statement: Ayida Wedo, Ayida-Weddo or Aida Wedo is a lwa of Haitian (haïtien) vodou.
claims.statement_id: Ayida Wedo, Ayida-Weddo, atau Aida Wedo adalah seorang lwa dalam vaudou Haiti (haïtien).
claims.quote: Ayida Wedo ou Ayida-Weddo ou Aida Wedo est un lwa du vaudou haïtien.

claims.statement: She is the goddess of the sky (ciel), clouds (nuages) and storms (tempêtes).
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah dewi langit (ciel), awan (nuages), dan badai (tempêtes).
claims.quote: Elle est la déesse Iwa du ciel, des nuages, et des tempêtes.

claims.statement: A rare merciful (miséricordieuse) deity in vodou culture, she often stands against Mami Wata to lift the curses (malédictions) Mami Wata casts on the unfaithful.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewi yang jarang berbelas kasih (miséricordieuse) dalam budaya vaudou, ia kerap melawan Mami Wata untuk mencabut kutukan (malédictions) yang dijatuhkan Mami Wata pada orang yang tidak setia.
claims.quote: Rare divinité miséricordieuse de la culture vaudou, elle se dresse souvent contre Mami Wata, pour lever les malédictions qu'elle jette sur les infidèles.

claims.statement: She is the wife (femme) of Damballa and represents wealth (richesse), luck (chance) and happiness (bonheur).
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah istri (femme) Damballa dan melambangkan kekayaan (richesse), keberuntungan (chance), dan kebahagiaan (bonheur).
claims.quote: Elle est, par ailleurs, la femme de Damballa, et représente la richesse, la chance, le bonheur

claims.statement: Like her husband, she lives near rivers (rivières) and prefers trees (arbres) of all kinds.
claims.statement_id: Seperti suaminya, ia tinggal dekat sungai (rivières) dan menyukai segala jenis pohon (arbres).
claims.quote: Comme son époux, elle vit près des rivières, et a une préférence pour les arbres de toutes sortes

claims.statement: She imitates the movements of the snake (couleuvre), and her symbols are the snake and the rainbow (arc-en-ciel).
claims.statement_id: Ia meniru gerakan ular (couleuvre), dan lambangnya adalah ular dan pelangi (arc-en-ciel).
claims.quote: Comme lui, elle imite les mouvements de la couleuvre. Ses symboles sont la couleuvre et aussi l'arc-en-ciel

claims.statement: According to Ellis, Anyi-ewo is the rainbow-god who manifests himself as a serpent and appears only when he is thirsty.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ellis, Anyi-ewo adalah dewa pelangi orang Ewe yang menampakkan diri dalam wujud ular dan hanya muncul ketika haus.
claims.quote: Anyi-ewo is the rainbow-god, who manifests himself in the form of a serpent, and only appears, it is believed, when he is thirsty and requires

claims.statement: He drinks prodigious quantities of water, and all that he spills falls like rain.
claims.statement_id: Ia meminum air dalam jumlah luar biasa, dan semua yang tumpah jatuh sebagai hujan.
claims.quote: He drinks prodigious quantities of water, and all that he spills falls down like rain.

claims.statement: In Whydah and Porto Novo the god appears to have another name, which Captain Burton writes Aydo-whe-do.
claims.statement_id: Di Whydah dan Porto Novo dewa ini tampaknya punya nama lain, yang ditulis Captain Burton sebagai Aydo-whe-do.
claims.quote: In Whydah and Porto Novo he appears to have another name, which Captain Burton writes Aydo-whe-do

claims.statement: Popo beads (aggry-beads) are believed to be made by Anyi-ewo.
claims.statement_id: Manik-manik Popo (aggry-beads) dipercaya dibuat oleh Anyi-ewo.
claims.quote: are believed to be made by Anyi-ewo

claims.statement: The Kongamato is a pterosaur-like cryptid reportedly seen by indigenous people and researchers in the Jiundu Swamps in the Mwinilunga district of western Zambia, Angola, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
claims.statement_id: Kongamato adalah kriptid mirip pterosaurus yang dilaporkan dilihat oleh penduduk asli dan para peneliti di Rawa Jiundu, distrik Mwinilunga, Zambia bagian barat, Angola, dan Republik Demokratik Kongo.
claims.quote: is a pterosaurlike cryptid reportedly seen by members of the indigenous population and researchers in the Jiundu Swamps in the Mwinilunga district of western Zambia, Angola, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

claims.statement: Further descriptions note that it has no feathers, smooth and mostly reddish skin, and a toothy beak.
claims.statement_id: Deskripsi lanjutan menyebut makhluk ini tanpa bulu, berkulit halus yang sebagian besar kemerahan, dan berparuh bergigi.
claims.quote: Further descriptions note a lack of feathers, smooth and mainly reddish skin, as well as a toothy beak.

claims.statement: The kongamato is said to live around certain rivers and is considered very dangerous.
claims.statement_id: Kongamato dikatakan hidup di sekitar sungai-sungai tertentu dan dianggap sangat berbahaya.
claims.quote: The kongamato is said to live around certain rivers and is considered very dangerous.

claims.statement: Frank Melland describes the alleged creature in his 1923 book In Witch-Bound Africa.
claims.statement_id: Frank Melland menguraikan makhluk yang diklaim ini dalam bukunya tahun 1923, In Witch-Bound Africa.
claims.quote: Frank Melland describes the alleged creature in his 1923 book In Witch-Bound Africa.

claims.statement: Members of the Kaondé, on seeing an image in Melland's book, judged that the creature looked exactly like a pterosaur.
claims.statement_id: Anggota suku Kaondé, setelah melihat gambar dalam buku Melland, menyimpulkan bahwa makhluk itu tampak persis seperti pterosaurus.
claims.quote: Members of the Kaondé, upon seeing an image in Melland

claims.statement: Skeptics have argued that such sightings are most likely misidentifications of known animals with superficially prehistoric features.
claims.statement_id: Para skeptis berpendapat bahwa penampakan semacam ini kemungkinan besar salah mengenali hewan yang sudah dikenal yang tampak purba secara sepintas.
claims.quote: Skeptics have argued that such sightings are likely the misidentification of known fauna with superficially prehistoric features.

claims.statement: The speaker told Melland that the kongamato is more like a lizard with membranous wings like a bat than a bird.
claims.statement_id: Penutur menjelaskan kepada Melland bahwa kongamato lebih mirip kadal bersayap selaput seperti kelelawar daripada burung.
claims.quote: it is more like a lizard with membranous wings like a bat

claims.statement: According to the information Melland gathered, the wing-spread was from 4 to 7 feet and the general colour was red.
claims.statement_id: Menurut keterangan yang dikumpulkan Melland, rentang sayapnya 4 sampai 7 kaki dan warna umumnya merah.
claims.quote: wing-spread was from 4 to 7 feet across, that the general colour was red

claims.statement: No one ever saw a kongamato close and lived to tell the tale, so details such as teeth in the beak could not be confirmed.
claims.statement_id: Tidak seorang pun pernah melihat kongamato dari dekat lalu hidup untuk menceritakannya; karena itu detail seperti gigi di paruh tidak bisa dipastikan.
claims.quote: no one ever saw a kongamato close and lived to tell the tale

claims.statement: The people say it is invulnerable, will eat any missile thrown at it, and is immortal, so that no remains are ever found.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk mengatakan kongamato kebal, melahap lembing atau lemparan apa pun, dan abadi, sehingga tidak pernah ada sisa tubuhnya ditemukan.
claims.quote: it is invulnerable, will eat any missile thrown at it, and that it is immortal, so that no remains are ever found.

claims.statement: The people do not regard it as an unnatural thing like a mulombe, only as a very awful thing.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk tidak menganggapnya sesuatu yang tidak alami seperti mulombe, melainkan hanya sesuatu yang sangat mengerikan.
claims.quote: The natives do not consider it to be an unnatural thing like a mulombe, only a very awful thing

claims.statement: In the belief about the river-crossing charm, the kongamato is said to have the power of stopping the waters from flowing away, raising the water level suddenly and overwhelming the traveller.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan tentang jimat untuk menyeberang sungai, kongamato dikatakan mampu menghentikan aliran air sehingga permukaan air naik tiba-tiba dan menenggelamkan penyeberang.
claims.quote: has the power of stopping the waters from flowing away, thus causing a sudden rise in the water level, and overwhelming the passenger.

claims.statement: The latest known case is said to have killed two men and two women in the Mutanda River near Lufumatunga village, an event attributed to a kongamato.
claims.statement_id: Kasus terakhir yang diketahui disebut menewaskan dua lelaki dan dua perempuan di Sungai Mutanda dekat desa Lufumatunga; kasus ini dikaitkan dengan kongamato.
claims.quote: two men and two women were killed by a kongamato in the Mutanda River near to Lufumatunga village

claims.statement: Sceptics point out that when the people were killed the river was naturally in flood.
claims.statement_id: Para skeptis menunjukkan bahwa saat orang-orang itu tewas sungai memang sedang banjir secara alami.
claims.quote: Sceptics point out that when the said people were killed the river was naturally in flood

claims.statement: The second article describes it with no feathers, smooth skin coloured red or black (rot oder schwarz), and a long beak studded with teeth (Zähnen).
claims.statement_id: Artikel kedua menggambarkan makhluk itu tanpa bulu, berkulit halus berwarna merah atau hitam (rot oder schwarz), dan berparuh panjang penuh gigi (Zähnen).
claims.quote: Der Flugsaurier besitzt keine Federn, sondern eine glatte rot oder schwarz gefärbte Haut und einen langen Schnabel, gespickt mit Zähnen.

claims.statement: The second article suggests the sightings might be local stork species such as the shoebill (Schuhschnabel-Storch).
claims.statement_id: Artikel kedua menyebut penampakan itu mungkin berupa jenis bangau setempat seperti bangau paruh-sepatu (Schuhschnabel-Storch).
claims.quote: Es könnte sich eventuell um Sichtungen einheimischer Storcharten wie den Schuhschnabel-Storch, der in Zaires Sümpfen lebt, handeln.

claims.statement: Another explanation given by the second article is a large, as yet unclassified bat-like animal (Fledertier).
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan lain yang disebut artikel kedua ialah hewan kelelawar besar yang belum terklasifikasi (Fledertier).
claims.quote: Nach einer anderen Erklärung könnte es sich um ein noch nicht klassifiziertes großes Fledertier handeln.

claims.statement: In 1932, naturalist Gerald Russell and cryptozoologist Ivan T. Sanderson claimed to have sighted a kongamato together in Cameroon.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1932, naturalis Gerald Russell dan kriptozoolog Ivan T. Sanderson mengaku bersama-sama melihat kongamato di Kamerun.
claims.quote: In 1932, naturalist Gerald Russell and cryptozoologist Ivan T. Sanderson claimed to have sighted a kongamato together in Cameroon

claims.statement: In Nguni mythology, the tokoloshe (also tikoloshe, tikolosh, tonkolosh, tonkolosi, tokolotshe, thokolosi or hili) is a dwarf-like water spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nguni, tokoloshe (juga ditulis tikoloshe, tikolosh, tonkolosh, tonkolosi, tokolotshe, thokolosi, atau hili) adalah roh air yang bertubuh seperti kurcaci.
claims.quote: In Nguni mythology, the tokoloshe, tikoloshe, tikolosh, tonkolosh, tonkolosi, tokolotshe, thokolosi, or hili is a dwarf-like water spirit.

claims.statement: It is a mischievous and evil spirit that can become invisible by drinking water or swallowing a stone.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah roh nakal dan jahat yang dapat menjadi tak terlihat dengan meminum air atau menelan batu.
claims.quote: It is a mischievous and evil spirit that can become invisible by drinking water or swallowing a stone.

claims.statement: Tokoloshes are called upon by malevolent people to cause trouble for others.
claims.statement_id: Tokoloshe dipanggil oleh orang berniat jahat untuk menimbulkan masalah bagi orang lain.
claims.quote: Tokoloshes are called upon by malevolent people to cause trouble for others.

claims.statement: At its least harmful a tokoloshe is used to scare children, but its power extends to causing illness or even the death of the victim.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bentuk paling ringan, tokoloshe dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak, tetapi kekuatannya sampai menyebabkan penyakit atau bahkan kematian korban.
claims.quote: At its least harmful, a tokoloshe can be used to scare children, but its power extends to causing illness or even the death of the victim.

claims.statement: Protection against it includes traditional methods such as raising beds off the ground and the intervention of spiritual figures such as pastors with an apostolic calling or traditional healers (sangomas).
claims.statement_id: Perlindungan terhadapnya mencakup cara tradisional seperti meninggikan tempat tidur dari tanah serta campur tangan tokoh spiritual seperti pendeta bertitel apostolik atau tabib tradisional (sangoma).
claims.quote: Protection against them includes traditional methods such as raising beds off the ground and interventions by spiritual figures like pastors with an apostolic calling or traditional healers (sangomas)

claims.statement: In the account of its creation, the witch doctor finds a dead body to possess, pierces the eye sockets and brain with a hot iron rod so the body cannot think for itself, and sprinkles it with a special powder that shrinks the body.
claims.statement_id: Dalam uraian tentang cara menciptakannya, dukun jahat mencari mayat untuk dirasuki, menusuk rongga mata dan otaknya dengan batang besi panas agar tubuh itu tidak berpikir sendiri, lalu menaburinya bubuk khusus yang menyusutkan tubuh.
claims.quote: The witch doctor locates a dead body to possess, piercing the eye sockets and brain with a hot iron rod to prevent the body from thinking for itself, and sprinkling it with a special powder that shrinks the body.

claims.statement: According to legend, the only way to keep the tokoloshe away at night is to put a few bricks beneath each leg of one's bed.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, satu-satunya cara menjauhkan tokoloshe pada malam hari adalah menaruh beberapa bata di bawah tiap kaki tempat tidur.
claims.quote: According to legend, the only way to keep the tokoloshe away at night is to put a few bricks beneath each leg of one's bed.

claims.statement: The dictionary defines the tokoloshe in African folklore as a mischievous and lascivious hairy water-sprite or goblin, also called hili.
claims.statement_id: Kamus mendefinisikan tokoloshe dalam cerita rakyat Afrika sebagai peri air atau goblin berbulu yang nakal dan mesum; disebut juga hili.
claims.quote: In African folklore: a mischievous and lascivious hairy water-sprite or goblin; hili.

claims.statement: Origin per the dictionary: utokoloshe in isiZulu, uthikoloshe in isiXhosa, and thökölösi, thikoloshi and tikoloshi in Sotho.
claims.statement_id: Asal kata dalam kamus: utokoloshe dalam isiZulu, uthikoloshe dalam isiXhosa, serta thökölösi, thikoloshi, dan tikoloshi dalam bahasa Sotho.
claims.quote: IsiZulu utokoloshe, isiXhosa uthikoloshe, Sotho thökölösi, thikoloshi, tikoloshi.

claims.statement: One citation in the dictionary says the hili are said to be a race of faun-like dwarfish male creatures who dwell in deep pools and among the reeds and rushes along the banks of flowing rivers.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu kutipan dalam kamus menyebut hili dikatakan sebagai ras makhluk jantan kerdil mirip faun yang tinggal di kolam dalam dan di antara alang-alang di tepi sungai yang mengalir.
claims.quote: they are said to be a race of faun-like, dwarfish male creatures ... who dwell in deep pools and among the reeds and rushes along the banks of flowing rivers.

claims.statement: Another citation in the dictionary describes thikoloshe as a small hairy being with a baboon-like face and the form of a man.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan lain dalam kamus menyebut thikoloshe sebagai makhluk kecil berbulu berwajah mirip babun dan berbentuk seperti manusia.
claims.quote: thikoloshe, a small hairy being with baboon-like face, having the form of a man

claims.statement: A third citation in the dictionary says the tikoloshe is supposed to be an evil spirit which takes the shape of a small man.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan lain lagi dalam kamus menyebut tikoloshe dianggap roh jahat yang berwujud lelaki kecil.
claims.quote: Tikoloshe is supposed to be an evil spirit which takes the shape of a small man.

claims.statement: The third article places the tokoloshe in Zulu mythology (zouloue) and says it can become invisible by swallowing a pebble (galet).
claims.statement_id: Artikel ketiga menyebut tokoloshe ada dalam mitologi Zulu (zouloue) dan dapat menjadi tak terlihat dengan menelan kerikil (galet).
claims.quote: dans la mythologie zouloue. Il peut devenir invisible en avalant un galet.

claims.statement: Olokun is a West African deity associated with the sea and other waters, wealth and fertility.
claims.statement_id: Olokun adalah dewa Afrika Barat yang dikaitkan dengan laut dan perairan lain, kekayaan, dan kesuburan.
claims.quote: Olokun is a West African deity associated with the sea and other waters, wealth and fertility.

claims.statement: Olokun is documented in Yoruba, Edo, Esan and Urhobo traditions and in some western Igbo and coastal Ijaw communities.
claims.statement_id: Olokun tercatat dalam tradisi Yoruba, Edo, Esan, dan Urhobo, serta di sebagian komunitas Igbo barat dan Ijaw pesisir.
claims.quote: Olokun is documented in the traditions of the Yoruba, Edo, Esan and Urhobo, as well as in some western Igbo and coastal Ijaw communities.

claims.statement: In some western Igbo and Urhobo communities, Olokun is called Onoku.
claims.statement_id: Di sebagian komunitas Igbo barat dan Urhobo, Olokun disebut Onoku.
claims.quote: In some western Igbo and Urhobo communities, Olokun is called Onoku.

claims.statement: The historical origins of Olokun worship remain uncertain.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul historis pemujaan Olokun masih belum pasti.
claims.quote: The historical origins of Olokun worship remain uncertain.

claims.statement: Olokun also appears in religions of the African diaspora, including Santería and Candomblé.
claims.statement_id: Olokun juga muncul dalam agama-agama diaspora Afrika, termasuk Santería dan Candomblé.
claims.quote: Olokun also appears in religions of the African diaspora, including Santería and Candomblé.

claims.statement: Depending on the tradition, Olokun may be described as female, male or androgynous.
claims.statement_id: Bergantung pada tradisinya, Olokun dapat digambarkan sebagai perempuan, laki-laki, atau androgini.
claims.quote: Depending on the tradition, Olokun may be described as female, male or androgynous.

claims.statement: In one Yoruba account from Ile-Ife, Olokun was Oduduwa's wife and became the sea after leaving him when he took another wife.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah Yoruba dari Ile-Ife, Olokun adalah istri Oduduwa dan menjadi laut setelah meninggalkannya ketika ia mengambil istri lain.
claims.quote: In one Yoruba account from Ile-Ife, Olokun was Oduduwa's wife and became the sea after leaving him when he took another wife.

claims.statement: In Edo traditions of the Benin Kingdom, Olokun is regarded as the senior son of Osanobua and is associated with the sea, human fertility, children and wealth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Edo di Kerajaan Benin (Benin Kingdom), Olokun dianggap putra sulung Osanobua dan dikaitkan dengan laut, kesuburan manusia, anak-anak, dan kekayaan.
claims.quote: In Edo traditions of the Benin Kingdom, Olokun is regarded as the senior son of Osanobua and is associated with the sea, human fertility, children and wealth.

claims.statement: Among the Esan, Olokun is also called Onokun and was worshipped especially by women seeking fertility and wealth.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Esan, Olokun juga disebut Onokun dan terutama dipuja perempuan yang mencari kesuburan dan kekayaan.
claims.quote: Among the Esan, Olokun is also called Onokun and was worshipped especially by women seeking fertility and wealth.

claims.statement: To establish an Onokun shrine, a woman gave a priestess a white goat, a white fowl and white cloth; the ceremony included fourteen days of dancing, and worshippers sometimes entered possession trances.
claims.statement_id: Untuk mendirikan tempat suci Onokun, seorang perempuan memberi pendeta perempuan seekor kambing putih, unggas putih, dan kain putih; upacaranya mencakup empat belas hari tarian, dan pemuja kadang mengalami trans kerasukan.
claims.quote: To establish an Onokun shrine, a woman provided a priestess with a white goat, a white fowl and white cloth; the ceremony included fourteen days of dancing. Worshippers sometimes entered possession trances.

claims.statement: Among the Itsekiri, Umale okun is the deity of the sea, and a small fish called ogiden was believed to be its messenger.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Itsekiri, Umale okun adalah dewa laut, dan seekor ikan kecil bernama ogiden dipercaya sebagai utusannya.
claims.quote: Among the Itsekiri, Umale okun is the deity of the sea. ... A small fish called ogiden was believed to be its messenger.

claims.statement: At Ogulaha, worshippers hold an annual festival by the Atlantic Ocean to ward off floods.
claims.statement_id: Di Ogulaha, para pemuja mengadakan festival tahunan di tepi Samudra Atlantik (Atlantic Ocean) untuk menangkal banjir.
claims.quote: At Ogulaha, worshippers hold an annual festival by the Atlantic Ocean to ward off floods.

claims.statement: In Brazil, Olokun is revered in some Candomblé terreiros, although Iemanjá became more prominent as a sea deity.
claims.statement_id: Di Brasil (Brazil), Olokun dihormati di sebagian terreiro Candomblé, walaupun Iemanjá menjadi dewi laut yang lebih menonjol.
claims.quote: In Brazil, Olokun is revered in some Candomblé terreiros, although Iemanjá became more prominent as a sea deity.

claims.statement: In Santería, Olokun is associated with the depths of the ocean and its hidden riches; some devotees see Olokun and Yemayá as aspects of the same orisha, others as spouses.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Santería, Olokun dikaitkan dengan kedalaman samudra dan kekayaannya yang tersembunyi; sebagian pemuja memandang Olokun dan Yemayá sebagai aspek orisha yang sama, sedangkan yang lain menganggap mereka suami-istri.
claims.quote: In Santería, Olokun is associated with the depths of the ocean and its hidden riches. ... Some devotees see Olokun and Yemayá as aspects of the same orisha, while others regard them as spouses.

claims.statement: The second source calls Olokun a river goddess associated with wealth and the provision of children, a traditional cult common to most of southern Nigeria.
claims.statement_id: Sumber kedua menyebut Olokun dewi sungai (river goddess) yang dikaitkan dengan kekayaan dan pemberian anak, dalam pemujaan tradisional yang umum di sebagian besar Nigeria selatan (southern Nigeria).
claims.quote: is a river goddess associated with wealth and the provision of children. It is a traditional cult common to most parts of southern Nigeria.

claims.statement: In Benin culture, Olokun can be looked upon as a god or goddess of the sea.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya Benin, Olokun dapat dipandang sebagai dewa atau dewi laut.
claims.quote: In Benin culture, Olokun can be looked upon as a god or goddess of the sea.

claims.statement: Oral tradition tells of a battle between Olokun and the Oba in which Olokun's possessions were stripped.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi lisan menceritakan pertempuran antara Olokun dan Oba yang membuat harta Olokun dilucuti.
claims.quote: Oral tradition tells us that Olokun and the Oba were engaged in a battle were Olokun’s possessions was stripped.

claims.statement: Ben-Amos suggests that Olokun, at least by name, may be Yoruba in origin.
claims.statement_id: Ben-Amos berpendapat bahwa Olokun, setidaknya namanya, mungkin berasal dari Yoruba.
claims.quote: Ben-Amos also suggests that Olokun at least by name may be Yoruba in Origin.
