claims.statement_id: Orang yang diserangnya batuk darah (cough up blood) dan sering meninggal, sehingga tuberkulosis paru (pulmonary tuberculosis) dianggap ulah Impundulu.
claims.quote: People so attacked cough up blood and frequently die. In consequence, pulmonary tuberculosis is considered as the work of the Impundulu.

claims.statement: The flapping of its huge wings produces thunder, and lightning is caused by hot fat dripping from its breast to earth.
claims.statement_id: Kepakan sayapnya yang besar menimbulkan guruh (thunder), dan petir berasal dari lemak panas (hot fat) yang menetes dari dadanya ke bumi.
claims.quote: the flapping of its huge wings produces thunder, and lightning is caused by the hot fat which drips from its breast, falling to earth.

claims.statement: Impundulu, a lightning bird, appeared in the form of an extremely handsome man.
claims.statement_id: Impundulu dikenal sebagai burung petir yang menampakkan diri sebagai pria yang sangat tampan (extremely handsome man).
claims.quote: Impundulu, a lightning bird, who appeared in the form of an extremely handsome man.

claims.statement: So named because, according to Zulu lore, the bird is left behind on the ground when lightning strikes.
claims.statement_id: Burung ini dinamai demikian karena menurut kepercayaan Zulu ia tertinggal di tanah (left behind on the ground) saat petir menyambar.
claims.quote: So named because, according to Zulu lore, the bird is left behind on the ground when lightning strikes.

claims.statement: The Southern Sotho imagine the lightning bird as a hamerkop, the Venda as an eagle, and the peoples of the north-western Transvaal as a flamingo.
claims.statement_id: Wujud burung petir berbeda-beda: orang Sotho Selatan membayangkannya sebagai hamerkop, orang Venda sebagai elang (eagle), dan bangsa-bangsa di barat laut Transvaal sebagai flamingo.
claims.quote: the Southern Sotho imagine the lightning bird as a hamerkop, the Venda imagine it as an eagle, and the peoples of the north-western Transvaal imagine it as a flamingo

claims.statement: The Baronga identify the lightning-bird with a hawk called chimungu, believed to bury itself in the ground where it strikes.
claims.statement_id: Orang Baronga menyamakan burung petir dengan sejenis elang (hawk) bernama chimungu yang dipercaya membenamkan diri ke tanah di tempat ia menyambar.
claims.quote: The Baronga identify the lightning-bird with a hawk called chimungu, which is believed to bury itself in the ground where it strikes.

claims.statement: When it darts down as lightning, people only see the flash.
claims.statement_id: Saat burung itu menukik turun sebagai petir, orang hanya melihat kilatannya (flash).
claims.quote: When it darts down as lightning people only see the flash.

claims.statement: An Obambou, also Obambo or Obamba, is a supernatural being belonging to tribes of Central Africa.
claims.statement_id: Obambou, juga disebut Obambo atau Obamba, adalah makhluk gaib (supernatural being) milik suku-suku di Afrika Tengah (Central Africa).
claims.quote: An Obambou, also Obambo or Obamba, is a supernatural being belonging to tribes of Central Africa.

claims.statement: It is depicted as evil, with the power to do evil or good if it chooses, able to possess and cause sickness, or to want a home built for it.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan jahat (evil), mampu berbuat jahat maupun baik bila mau, dapat merasuki (possess) dan menyebabkan sakit, atau meminta dibuatkan rumah.
claims.quote: It is depicted as evil, possessing the power to do evil and to do good if it chooses, having the ability to possess and cause sickness, or to want a home built for them.

claims.statement: In some tribes an Obambou is referred to as a devil, or as the spirit of someone who was not buried correctly.
claims.statement_id: Di sebagian suku, Obambou disebut iblis (devil) atau arwah (spirit) orang yang tidak dikuburkan dengan benar.
claims.quote: In some African tribes, an Obambou is referred to as a devil, or as the spirit of someone who was not buried correctly.

claims.statement: The Commi tribe believed that when someone is severely ill an Obambou is a likely culprit, which can be determined by a doctor.
claims.statement_id: Suku Commi percaya bahwa bila seseorang sakit parah, Obambou kemungkinan penyebabnya, dan hal itu dapat ditentukan oleh seorang dukun (doctor).
claims.quote: The Commi tribe believed that when someone is severely ill, an Obambou is a likely culprit which can be determined by a doctor

claims.statement: The M'pongwe tribe believed a person can be born with the spirit known as an Obambou and be born insane.
claims.statement_id: Suku M'pongwe percaya seseorang dapat lahir bersama roh (spirit) Obambou dan lahir dalam keadaan gila (insane).
claims.quote: The M'pongwe tribe believed that a person can be born with the spirit known as an Obambou and be born insane.

claims.statement: In some tribes Obambou is married to a female spirit.
claims.statement_id: Di sebagian suku, Obambou dikatakan menikah (married) dengan roh perempuan (female spirit).
claims.quote: In some tribes, Obambou is married to a female spirit.

claims.statement: One of the Commi people's theories of disease is that Obambou (the devil) has got into the sick man, and while the devil remains in the body there is no hope of curing him.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu teori penyakit orang Commi adalah bahwa Obambou (iblis/devil) telah masuk ke tubuh orang sakit, dan selama ia tinggal di tubuh itu tidak ada harapan sembuh.
claims.quote: One of the Commi people's theories of disease is, that Obambou (the devil) has got into the sick man, and as long as the devil remains in the body there is no hope of curing the man.

claims.statement: This devil can only be driven out by noise: a great crowd surrounds the sick man, beats drums and kettles close to his head and fires guns close to his ears.
claims.statement_id: Iblis ini hanya dapat diusir dengan bunyi (noise): kerumunan besar mengelilingi orang sakit, memukul genderang dan ketel (drums and kettles) dekat kepalanya, dan menembakkan senapan (guns) dekat telinganya.
claims.quote: Now this devil is only to be driven out by noise, and accordingly a great crowd surround the sick man and beat drums and kettles close to his head, fire off guns close to his ears

claims.statement: Abambou is the devil of the Commi people; a wicked and mischievous fellow who often lives near graves and burial-grounds and is most comfortably lodged among the skeletons of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Abambou adalah iblis (devil) orang Commi; ia jahat dan usil, sering tinggal dekat kuburan (graves and burial-grounds), dan paling nyaman berdiam di antara kerangka orang mati.
claims.quote: Abambou is the devil of the Commi people. He is a wicked and mischievous fellow, who often lives near graves and burial-grounds, and is most comfortably lodged among the skeletons of the dead.

claims.statement: He takes occasional walks through the country and, if angry at anyone, has the power to cause sickness and death.
claims.statement_id: Ia sesekali berjalan-jalan melintasi negeri, dan bila marah kepada seseorang ia berkuasa menimbulkan sakit dan kematian (sickness and death).
claims.quote: He takes occasional walks through the country, and, if he gets angry at anyone, he has the power to cause sickness and death.

claims.statement: The Commi people cook food for him, deposit it in lonely places in the woods, and there address him flatteringly and ask him to be good to them.
claims.statement_id: Orang Commi memasak makanan (food) untuknya, menaruhnya di tempat sepi di hutan (woods), lalu menyapanya dengan sanjungan dan memintanya berbaik hati kepada mereka.
claims.quote: The Commi people cook food for him, which is deposited in lonely places in the woods, and there they address him in a flattering manner, and ask him to be good to them

claims.statement: In Aniambia there are two fetich-houses protected by two powerful spirits, Abambou and Mbiuri; the former is an evil spirit, a kind of devil, the latter beneficent.
claims.statement_id: Di Aniambia ada dua rumah jimat (fetich-houses) yang dilindungi dua roh berkuasa, Abambou dan Mbiuri; yang pertama roh jahat semacam iblis, yang kedua bersifat baik (beneficent).
claims.quote: There are two very curious fetich-houses in Aniambia, which enjoy the protection of two spirits of great power—Abambou and Mbiuri. The former is an evil spirit, a kind of devil; the latter, as far as I have been able to ascertain, is beneficent.

claims.statement: In M'pongwe belief, an evil spirit such as an Obambo, the soul of a man that has not been buried properly, can be born with a person.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan M'pongwe, roh jahat seperti Obambo, yaitu jiwa orang yang tidak dikuburkan dengan layak (not been buried properly), dapat lahir bersama seseorang.
claims.quote: or an Obambo, the soul of a man that has not been buried properly, has been born with him.

claims.statement: When the dead are weary of staying in the bush, they come for one of their people whom they most affect.
claims.statement_id: Bila orang mati sudah lelah tinggal di semak belukar (bush), mereka mendatangi salah seorang kerabat yang paling mereka sayangi.
claims.quote: When the dead are weary of staying in the bush, they come for one of their people whom they most affect.

claims.statement: The spirit says it is tired of dwelling in the bush and asks for a little house to be built in the town as close as possible to the visited person's own.
claims.statement_id: Arwah itu berkata bahwa ia lelah tinggal di semak (bush) dan meminta dibangunkan rumah kecil (little house) di kampung sedekat mungkin dengan rumah orang yang didatanginya.
claims.quote: I am tired of dwelling in the bush; please to build for me in the town a little house as close as possible to your own.

claims.statement: Next day the people go to the grave of the Obambo, or ghost, make a rude idol, and carry the bamboo bier of the body and some dust of the ground into a little hut near the house of the visited, draping a white cloth over the door.
claims.statement_id: Keesokan harinya orang pergi ke kubur Obambo (ghost), membuat berhala (idol) sederhana, lalu membawa usungan bambu (bamboo bier) jenazah dan sedikit debu kubur ke pondok kecil dekat rumah orang yang didatangi, dan pintunya ditutup kain putih (white cloth).
claims.quote: Then, next day, the people repair to the grave of the Obambo, or ghost, and make a rude idol; after which the bamboo bier on which the body is conveyed to the grave, and some of the dust of the ground, are carried into a little hut erected near the house of the visited, and a white cloth is draped over the door.

claims.statement: Aganjú (also known as Agayú or Aggayú in the African diaspora) is an Orisha in Yoruba religion and its descendant traditions in the Americas.
claims.statement_id: Aganjú (juga dikenal sebagai Agayú atau Aggayú di diaspora Afrika) adalah seorang Orisha dalam agama Yoruba dan tradisi turunannya di Amerika.
claims.quote: Aganjú (also known as Agayú or Aggayú in the African diaspora) is an Orisha in Yoruba religion and its descendant traditions in the Americas.

claims.statement: He is a primordial deity associated with the sun, fire, and the untamed wilderness.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah dewa purba yang dikaitkan dengan matahari, api, dan alam liar yang belum dijinakkan.
claims.quote: He is a primordial deity associated with the sun, fire, and the untamed wilderness.

claims.statement: In Nigeria and Benin, Aganjú is venerated as a deified warrior king originating from the town of Shaki in Oyo State.
claims.statement_id: Di Nigeria dan Benin, Aganjú dihormati sebagai raja pejuang yang didewakan dan berasal dari kota Shaki di Oyo State.
claims.quote: In Nigeria and Benin, Aganjú is venerated as a deified warrior king originating from the town of Shaki in Oyo State.

claims.statement: Unlike Shango, who is associated with thunder and lightning stones, Aganjú is said to fight with a sword, paralysis, and fire and heat.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari Shango yang dikaitkan dengan guntur dan batu petir, Aganjú dikatakan bertarung dengan pedang, kelumpuhan, serta api dan panas.
claims.quote: Unlike Shango, who is associated with thunder and lightning stones, Aganjú is said to fight with a sword, paralysis, and fire and heat.

claims.statement: In the Cuban tradition of Santería, Aganjú is associated with volcanoes and syncretized with Saint Christopher.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Santería, Aganjú dikaitkan dengan gunung berapi dan disinkretiskan dengan Saint Christopher.
claims.quote: In the Cuban tradition of Santería, Aganjú is associated with volcanoes and syncretized with Saint Christopher.

claims.statement: In Candomblé he is referred to as Xangô Aganjú and represents the raw, uncontrollable aspects of fire and the earth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Candomblé, ia disebut Xangô Aganjú dan melambangkan sisi api dan bumi yang mentah serta tak terkendali.
claims.quote: referred to as Xangô Aganjú. He represents the raw, uncontrollable aspects of fire and the earth.

claims.statement: Aganju was a legendary Alaafin, described in some oral traditions as the nephew of Shango and the son of Ajaka.
claims.statement_id: Aganju adalah seorang Alaafin legendaris yang dalam sebagian tradisi lisan digambarkan sebagai keponakan Shango dan putra Ajaka.
claims.quote: Aganju was a legendary Alaafin, described in some oral traditions as the nephew of Shango and the son of Ajaka.

claims.statement: In Yoruba (iorubá), aginjù (not Aganju) means an inhospitable place, a desert (deserto), or an impenetrable place.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Yoruba (iorubá), aginjù (bukan Aganju) berarti tempat yang tidak ramah, gurun (deserto), atau tempat yang tidak bisa ditembus.
claims.quote: Na língua iorubá, aginjù (não Aganju) significa localidade inóspita, um deserto ou local impenetrável.

claims.statement: Aganju is strongly associated with the orixá Xangô; in some traditions he is described as Xangô's father (pai), in others as his brother (irmão).
claims.statement_id: Aganju sangat terkait dengan orixá Xangô; dalam sebagian tradisi ia disebut ayah (pai) Xangô, dalam tradisi lain saudaranya (irmão).
claims.quote: Aganju está fortemente associado ao orixá Xangô. Em algumas tradições, Aganju é descrito como o pai de Xangô; em outras ele é descrito como seu irmão.

claims.statement: The son of Oroiña (hijo de Oroiña), he is considered by some to be the father (padre) of Shango and Orungán.
claims.statement_id: Anak Oroiña (hijo de Oroiña), ia dianggap oleh sebagian orang sebagai ayah (padre) Shango dan Orungán.
claims.quote: Hijo de Oroiña, es considerado por algunos como el padre de Shango y Orungán.

claims.statement: In this older record, Yemaja married her brother Aganju and bore a son named Orungan.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan lama ini, Yemaja menikahi saudara laki-lakinya, Aganju, dan melahirkan seorang putra bernama Orungan.
claims.quote: Yemaja married her brother Aganju, and bore a son named Orungan.

claims.statement: There is said to be an open space in front of the king's residence in Oyo where the god was formerly worshipped.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan ada sebuah lapangan terbuka di depan kediaman raja di Oyo, tempat sang dewa dahulu disembah.
claims.quote: there is said to be an open space in front of the king's residence in Oyo where the god was formerly worshipped

claims.statement: The Ninki Nanka is a legendary creature in folklore.
claims.statement_id: Ninki Nanka adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat (folklore).
claims.quote: A Ninki Nanka is a legendary creature in West African folklore.

claims.statement: The Ninki Nanka kept many people of the lower Gambia away from fertile swamps, rivers, hills and creeks; it was believed to inhabit swampy forests and caves.
claims.statement_id: Ninki Nanka membuat banyak orang di Gambia hilir menjauhi rawa, sungai, bukit, dan anak sungai yang subur; ia dipercaya menghuni hutan berawa dan gua (swampy forests and caves).
claims.quote: The Ninki Nanka kept many lower Gambians away from fertile swamps, rivers, hills, and creeks, and the creature was often believed to inhabit swampy forests and caves.

claims.statement: Various accounts describe it as a river or swamp dragon.
claims.statement_id: Berbagai kisah menggambarkannya sebagai naga sungai atau naga rawa (river or swamp dragon).
claims.quote: Various accounts have also described it as a river or swamp dragon.

claims.statement: Descriptions differ between tribes, but most say it is reptilian: a crocodile's head on a donkey's body or a hippopotamus-giraffe blend, sometimes simply a large snake.
claims.statement_id: Gambarannya berbeda antarsuku, tetapi kebanyakan menyebutnya reptil: berkepala buaya dengan tubuh keledai atau campuran kuda nil dan jerapah (hippopotamus and giraffe), kadang sekadar ular besar.
claims.quote: Descriptions of the creature vary across different tribes, but most contend that the animal is reptilian. It is depicted as having the head of a crocodile with the body of a donkey or a blend of hippopotamus and giraffe, and sometimes simply as a large snake.

claims.statement: Some accounts describe a 9m (30-foot) marsh-dwelling beast with a crocodile-like body, mirror-like scales, a giraffe-like long neck, a horse's head and three horns.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kisah menyebutnya binatang rawa sepanjang 9 m (30-foot) bertubuh seperti buaya, bersisik seperti cermin, berleher panjang seperti jerapah, berkepala kuda, dan bertanduk tiga.
claims.quote: Some accounts of the legendary creature describe it as a 9m or 30-foot long marsh-dwelling beast having a body like that of a crocodile, mirror-like scales and long neck like that of a giraffe with a horse's head along with three horns.

claims.statement: Most descriptions credit it with a fatal stare, akin to Medusa, causing death on eye contact; folklore advises carrying mirrors to deflect its gaze.
claims.statement_id: Hampir semua kisah menyebut tatapannya mematikan (fatal stare), seperti Medusa; cerita rakyat menganjurkan membawa cermin untuk menangkis tatapannya.
claims.quote: Common across descriptions is its believed fatal stare, akin to Medusa, which is said to cause death upon eye contact. Folklore advises carrying mirrors to deflect its gaze.

claims.statement: It is also believed able to camouflage itself with scales that shimmer in various colours, and is said to be extremely large and very dangerous.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dipercaya mampu menyamarkan diri (camouflage) dengan sisik yang berkilau aneka warna, serta disebut sangat besar dan sangat berbahaya.
claims.quote: Another belief is that it has the ability to camouflage, using its scales which shimmer in various colors. ... The animal is said to be extremely large and very dangerous.

claims.statement: A 1906 commissioner's report likens it to a gigantic crowned serpent living in the thickest bush; seeing its body brings dangerous sickness, while seeing its eyes or crown means instant death.
claims.statement_id: Laporan komisaris 1906 menyebutnya mirip ular raksasa bermahkota (crowned serpent) yang tinggal di semak paling lebat; melihat tubuhnya membawa penyakit berbahaya, melihat mata atau mahkotanya berarti kematian seketika.
claims.quote: A 1906 commissioner's report describes the creature: ... this is supposed to resemble a gigantic crowned serpent which resides in the thickest bush. If a native sees the body of this creature he believes that he will be afflicted with dangerous sickness but that if he sees the eyes or crown it means instantaneous death.

claims.statement: Evil spirits such as the Ninki Nanka were believed to bring drought or famine.
claims.statement_id: Roh jahat (evil spirits) seperti Ninki Nanka dipercaya mendatangkan kekeringan atau kelaparan.
claims.quote: Evil spirits such as the Ninki Nanka were believed to bring about drought or famine.

claims.statement: The Ninki Nanka appears in the 2021 fantasy novel Skin of the Sea by Natasha Bowen and is also depicted in a 2022 fantasy novel.
claims.statement_id: Ninki Nanka muncul dalam novel fantasi Skin of the Sea karya Natasha Bowen (2021) dan digambarkan pula dalam sebuah novel fantasi tahun 2022.
claims.quote: Ninki Nanka are featured in the 2021 fantasy novel, Skin of the Sea by Natasha Bowen. It is also depicted in the 2022 fantasy novel,

claims.statement: Ninki-Nanka (also spelled Ninkinanka) is a fabulous creature (Fabelwesen) of Gambia, compared with the Loch Ness monster.
claims.statement_id: Ninki-Nanka (ejaan lain Ninkinanka) adalah makhluk dongeng (Fabelwesen) di Gambia, yang dibandingkan dengan monster Loch Ness.
claims.quote: Ninki-Nanka (andere Schreibweise Ninkinanka) ist ein Fabelwesen im westafrikanischen Staat Gambia, vergleichbar mit dem Ungeheuer von Loch Ness.

claims.statement: It is described as an animal with a long, scaly body and a horse-like head (Pferd), sometimes as crocodile-like; lengths of up to 30 metres have been given.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai hewan bertubuh panjang bersisik (Schuppen) dengan kepala mirip kuda (Pferd), kadang mirip buaya; panjangnya disebut hingga 30 meter.
claims.quote: Beschrieben wird es als Tier mit einem langen, mit Schuppen besetzten Körper und einem Kopf ähnlich einem Pferd. Aber es wird auch als krokodilähnlich beschrieben. Längenangaben sind bis 30 Meter gemacht worden.

claims.statement: In July 2006 a group of researchers from the Centre for Fortean Zoology mounted an expedition to Gambia in search of Ninki Nanka.
claims.statement_id: Pada Juli 2006 sekelompok peneliti dari Centre for Fortean Zoology melakukan ekspedisi ke Gambia untuk mencari Ninki Nanka.
claims.quote: Im Juli 2006 führte eine Gruppe von britischen Forschern des Centre for Fortean Zoology auf der Suche nach Ninki Nanka eine Expedition nach Gambia durch.

claims.statement: The Mandinka people also describe the Ninki Nanka as a dragon.
claims.statement_id: Orang Mandinka juga menggambarkan Ninki Nanka sebagai naga (dragon).
claims.quote: The Mandinka people have also described the Ninki Nanka as a dragon with a

claims.statement: Oshumare is an Orisha, the divine serpent spirit of the rainbow.
claims.statement_id: Oshumare adalah seorang Orisha, roh ular ilahi pelangi (divine serpent spirit of the rainbow).
claims.quote: Oshumare is the divine serpent spirit of the rainbow. ... A common belief of the Oshumare is that it is both male and female.

claims.statement: Oshumare is commonly believed to be both male and female, and is known as a symbol of creation, human reproduction and the link between the everyday world and that of the ancestors.
claims.statement_id: Oshumare umum dipercaya bersifat laki-laki sekaligus perempuan (male and female), dan dikenal sebagai lambang penciptaan, reproduksi manusia, serta penghubung dunia sehari-hari dengan dunia leluhur.
claims.quote: A common belief of the Oshumare is that it is both male and female. It is also known as a symbol of creation, human reproduction and the link between the world of the mundane and that of the ancestors.

claims.statement: Oshumaré is an Orisha in the Yoruba religion and the religions derived from it, such as Candomblé and Santería.
claims.statement_id: Oshumaré adalah Orisha dalam agama Yoruba dan agama-agama turunannya seperti Candomblé dan Santería.
claims.quote: ist ein Orisha in der Religion der Yoruba und der darauf beruhenden afroamerikanischen Religionen wie dem brasilianischen Candomblé oder der kubanischen Santería.

claims.statement: In syncretism with Catholic saints he is venerated as Bartholomäus (Bartholomew), and in Voodoo he is identified with Damballah.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sinkretisme dengan orang suci Katolik ia dihormati sebagai Bartholomäus, dan dalam Voodoo ia disamakan dengan Damballah.
claims.quote: In der synkretistischen Verbindung mit katholischen Heiligen wird er als Bartholomäus verehrt, im Voodoo wird er mit Damballah identifiziert.

claims.statement: He is the Orisha of the rainbow (Regenbogen), who rises as a great snake (Schlange) from beneath the world to drink water in the clouds.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah Orisha pelangi (Regenbogen) yang naik sebagai ular besar (Schlange) dari bagian bawah dunia untuk minum air di awan.
claims.quote: Er ist der Orisha des Regenbogens, der als große Schlange von der Unterseite der Welt aufsteigt, um in den Wolken Wasser zu trinken.

claims.statement: He rules the seasons, rain (Regen) and drought, and is responsible for hunger and prosperity.
claims.statement_id: Ia menguasai musim, hujan (Regen), dan kemarau, serta bertanggung jawab atas kelaparan dan kemakmuran.
claims.quote: Er beherrscht die Jahreszeiten, den Regen und die Trockenheit, und ist für Hunger und Wohlstand zuständig

claims.statement: He is regarded as the son of Nana Buruku, twin brother of Babalú Ayé, and the crown of Yemayá.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap putra Nana Buruku, saudara kembar Babalú Ayé, dan mahkota Yemayá.
claims.quote: Er gilt als Sohn der Nana Buruku und Zwillingsbruder des Babalú Ayé sowie als Krone der Yemayá.

claims.statement: He is said to have helped cure the blindness (ceguera) of Olodumare, who then offered him a home in the Orun.
claims.statement_id: Konon ia membantu menyembuhkan kebutaan (ceguera) Olodumare, lalu Olodumare menawarinya tinggal di Orun.
claims.quote: Se dice que ayudó a curar la ceguera de Olodumare, cuando este le ofreció residir en el Orun.

claims.statement: He represents the union of earth and sky (tierra y el cielo), is androgynous, and his double nature shows in the colours red (masculine) and blue (feminine).
claims.statement_id: Ia melambangkan penyatuan bumi dan langit (tierra y el cielo), bersifat androgini, dan sifat gandanya tampak pada warna merah (maskulin) dan biru (feminin).
claims.quote: Es la representación, la unión entre la tierra y el cielo, su equilibrio, balancea la unión entre los hombres y los Orishas, es andrógino, este doble aspecto se hace presente en los colores rojo (masculino) y azul (femenino).

claims.statement: He is called the son of Babalú Ayé (Hijo de Babalú Ayé), and brother of Irokó and Babalú Ayé.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut putra Babalú Ayé (Hijo de Babalú Ayé), saudara Irokó dan Babalú Ayé.
claims.quote: Hijo de Babalú Ayé, hermano de Irokó y de Babalú Ayé.

claims.statement: His emblem is pictured as a circular serpent (serpiente circular) biting its own tail, read as what keeps the earth from being destroyed.
claims.statement_id: Lambangnya dibayangkan sebagai ular melingkar yang menggigit ekornya sendiri (serpiente circular), yang ditafsirkan sebagai penjaga agar bumi tidak hancur.
claims.quote: Es visualizada como una serpiente circular la cual se muerde su propia cola. Se interpreta en este aspecto como lo que evita que la tierra se destruya o se aniquile.

claims.statement: According to some natives, Oshumare, the Rainbow, is the servant of Shango whose task is to carry water from the earth to the palace in the clouds.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian penduduk, Oshumare, sang Pelangi, adalah pelayan Shango yang bertugas mengangkat air dari bumi ke istana di awan.
claims.quote: According to some natives, Oshumare, the Rainbow, is the servant of Shango, his office being to take up water from the earth to the palace in the clouds.

claims.statement: He is the Rainbow-god, the Great Snake of the Underneath, who at times rises above the edge of the earth to drink water from the sky.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah dewa Pelangi, Ular Besar dari Bawah (Great Snake of the Underneath), yang sesekali naik di atas tepi bumi untuk minum air dari langit.
claims.quote: is the Rainbow-god, the Great Snake of the Underneath, who comes up at times above the edge of the earth to drink water from the sky.

claims.statement: A kind of python, called ere by the Yorubas, is the rainbow-god's messenger and is sacred to him.
claims.statement_id: Sejenis ular piton yang oleh orang Yoruba disebut ere adalah utusan dewa pelangi dan dikeramatkan baginya.
claims.quote: A variety of the python, called by the Yorubas ere, is the messenger of the rainbow-god, and is sacred to him.

claims.statement: Oshunmare or Oshumare (Òṣùmàrè) is a deity (deidad) of the Yoruba pantheon.
claims.statement_id: Oshunmare atau Oshumare (Òṣùmàrè) adalah dewa (deidad) dalam panteon Yoruba.
claims.quote: Oshunmare u Oshumare (del idioma yoruba: Òṣùmàrè) es una deidad del Panteón Yoruba, pertenece a la Religión Yoruba.

claims.statement: The aigamuxa are legendary creatures of the Khoikhoi people.
claims.statement_id: Aigamuxa adalah makhluk legenda orang Khoikhoi (Khoikhoi people).
claims.quote: are legendary creatures of the Khoikhoi people.

claims.statement: Its main food is humans, whom it takes for zebras and eats with its extremely elongated teeth.
claims.statement_id: Makanan utamanya manusia, yang dianggapnya zebra, dan dimakannya dengan gigi yang sangat panjang (elongated teeth).
claims.quote: Its main diet is humans, which it regards as zebras, and eats with its extremely elongated teeth.

claims.statement: They are said to target lone desert travellers at night.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini konon mengincar pengembara gurun yang sendirian pada malam hari (desert travelers at night).
claims.quote: The bushmen are said to target lone desert travelers at night.

claims.statement: The monster is said to have eyes on its feet, so it cannot see its prey while hunting; to see, it must stand on its hands or head, or lie in the sand.
claims.statement_id: Monster ini konon bermata di kakinya (eyes on its feet) sehingga tidak dapat melihat mangsanya saat berburu; untuk melihat ia harus bertumpu pada tangan atau kepala, atau berbaring di pasir.
claims.quote: The monster is said to have eyes on its feet, meaning that it cannot see the humans it preys upon as it hunts. In order to see, it must stand on its hands or head, or lie in the sand.

claims.statement: Tales of the aigamuxa were collected from the Khoikhoi by Leonhard Schultze-Jena for his book Aus Namaland und Kalahari.
claims.statement_id: Kisah-kisah aigamuxa dikumpulkan dari orang Khoikhoi oleh Leonhard Schultze-Jena untuk bukunya Aus Namaland und Kalahari.
claims.quote: Tales of the aigamuxa were notably collected from the Khoikhoi people by Leonhard Schultze-Jena for his book Aus Namaland und Kalahari.

claims.statement: There are many stories of clever humans who escaped the Aigamuxa, which are ferocious but stupid (feroci ma stupidi).
claims.statement_id: Ada banyak cerita tentang manusia cerdik yang berhasil lolos dari Aigamuxa, yang buas tetapi bodoh (feroci ma stupidi).
claims.quote: Ci sono molte storie riguardanti degli umani intelligenti che sono riusciti a sfuggire agli Aigamuxa, feroci ma stupidi.

claims.statement: In one of them the rascal Jackal scattered tobacco (tabacco) powder that got into their eyes, letting him escape.
claims.statement_id: Dalam salah satu cerita, si licik Jackal menaburkan bubuk tembakau (tabacco) yang masuk ke mata mereka sehingga ia dapat melarikan diri.
claims.quote: In una di queste il farabutto Jackal cosparse il terreno di polvere di tabacco ed esso finì nei loro occhi, permettendogli di fuggire.

claims.statement: The Aigamuxa have their eyes at ankle height (caviglie) and live in the desert (deserto).
claims.statement_id: Mata Aigamuxa terletak setinggi pergelangan kaki (caviglie), dan mereka hidup di gurun (deserto).
claims.quote: Gli Aigamuxa, i cui occhi si ritrovano all'altezza delle caviglie, vivono nel deserto

claims.statement: The third article describes it as a man-eating monster (людоед) that looks like a big, thin ape (обезьяна) with long fangs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam artikel ketiga ia digambarkan sebagai monster pemakan manusia (людоед) yang tampak seperti kera (обезьяна) besar dan kurus bertaring panjang.
claims.quote: в готтентотской мифологии, чудовище-людоед, выглядящее как большая, худая обезьяна с длинными клыками

claims.statement: According to legend, the aigamuxa (айгамукса) hides behind sand dunes and lies in wait for careless travellers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, aigamuxa (айгамукса) bersembunyi di balik bukit pasir dan menyergap pengembara yang lengah.
claims.quote: Согласно легендам, айгамукса прячется за песчаными дюнами и подстерегает беспечных и неосторожных путешественников.

claims.statement: The aigamuxa (айгамуксу) was described as forever hungry, because its clumsiness meant it seldom managed to catch and eat a person.
claims.statement_id: Aigamuxa (айгамуксу) dilukiskan selalu lapar karena kecanggungannya membuatnya jarang berhasil menangkap dan memakan manusia.
claims.quote: описывали айгамуксу как вечно голодное существо, поскольку из-за своей неповоротливости чудовищу редко удавалось схватить и съесть человека

claims.statement: In the world of legend, far in the interior of the land, there lives a fabulous creature (Fabelwesen).
claims.statement_id: Dalam dunia legenda, jauh di pedalaman negeri hidup suatu makhluk dongeng (Fabelwesen).
claims.quote: Weit im Innern des Landes lebt in der Sagenwelt ein Fabelwesen, das die Hottentotten

claims.statement: Its name comes from where its eyes (Augen) are: not in its face but on the top of its feet (Rücken der Füße).
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari letak matanya (Augen), yang bukan di wajah melainkan di punggung kaki (Rücken der Füße).
claims.quote: weil es seine Augen (mütti) nicht im Gesicht, sondern auf dem Rücken (fgäfb) der Füße (i=aiti) hat.

claims.statement: These creatures live together in groups and hunt people (Menschen), whom they take for zebras, to tear them with finger-long (fingerlangen) teeth.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk-makhluk ini hidup berkelompok dan memburu manusia (Menschen) yang mereka kira zebra, untuk dicabik dengan gigi sepanjang jari (fingerlangen).
claims.quote: Diese Fabelwesen leben gesellig beisammen und machen auf Menschen, die sie für Zebras halten, Jagd, um sie mit ihren fingerlangen, spitzen,

claims.statement: In the tales they usually appear so human-like (menschenähnlich) that they can deceive their victims about their true nature.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah-kisah, mereka biasanya tampil begitu mirip manusia (menschenähnlich) sehingga dapat menipu korban tentang wujud aslinya.
claims.quote: er läßt sie meist so menschenähnlich auftreten, daß sie ihre Opfer über ihre wahre Natur so lange täuschen können bis ein

claims.statement: The discovery of the foot-eyes (Fußaugen) of Aigamuchab is credited to the Jackal (Schakal) in Sage VI.
claims.statement_id: Penemuan mata di kaki (Fußaugen) Aigamuchab adalah jasa si Serigala (Schakal) dalam Sage VI.
claims.quote: Die Entdeckung der Fußaugen des Aigamuchab ist des Schakals Verdienst (Sage VI).

claims.statement: When his pipe had been filled, he scattered tobacco (Tabak).
claims.statement_id: Setelah pipanya diisi, ia menaburkan tembakau (Tabak).
claims.quote: Und als ihm die Pfeife gestopft worden war, streute (tsoro) er Tabak

claims.statement: The Aziza are a kind of beneficent supernatural race in Dahomey mythology.
claims.statement_id: Aziza adalah sejenis bangsa gaib yang baik hati (beneficent supernatural race) dalam mitologi Dahomey.
claims.quote: The Aziza are a type of beneficent supernatural race in West African (specifically, Dahomey) mythology.

claims.statement: They live in the forest, give good magic to hunters, and are known to have given people practical and spiritual knowledge, including the use of fire.
claims.statement_id: Mereka tinggal di hutan, memberi sihir baik kepada para pemburu, dan dikenal memberi manusia pengetahuan praktis dan spiritual, termasuk cara memakai api (fire).
claims.quote: Living in the forest, they provide good magic for hunters. They are also known to have given practical and spiritual knowledge to people (including knowledge of the use of fire).

claims.statement: The Aziza are described as little people said to live in anthills and silk-cotton trees.
claims.statement_id: Aziza digambarkan sebagai orang-orang kecil (little people) yang tinggal di sarang semut dan pohon kapuk (silk-cotton trees).
claims.quote: The Aziza are described as little people and are said to live in anthills and silk-cotton trees.

claims.statement: A plant genus, Aziza, has been named in their honour.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah genus tumbuhan (plant genus) dinamai Aziza untuk menghormati mereka.
claims.quote: The plant genus Aziza has been named in their honour.

claims.statement: Aziza is also a god of the Urhobo people of the Western Niger Delta of Nigeria.
claims.statement_id: Aziza juga merupakan dewa (god) orang Urhobo di bagian barat Delta Niger, Nigeria.
claims.quote: Aziza is also a god of the Urhobo people of the Western Niger Delta of Nigeria.

claims.statement: The Aziza are a race of benevolent fairies (fées bienfaisantes).
claims.statement_id: Aziza adalah bangsa peri yang baik hati (fées bienfaisantes).
claims.quote: sont une race de fées bienfaisantes d'Afrique

claims.statement: They live in the forest (forêt) and use their magic to bring luck to hunters (chasseurs).
claims.statement_id: Mereka tinggal di hutan (forêt) dan dengan sihirnya memberi keberuntungan kepada pemburu (chasseurs).
claims.quote: Elles vivent dans la forêt, où elles offrent de la chance aux chasseurs grâce à leur magie.

claims.statement: They are said to have introduced hunters to the art of music and song (musique et chanson).
claims.statement_id: Mereka konon mengenalkan para pemburu pada seni musik dan nyanyian (musique et chanson).
claims.quote: elles auraient initié des chasseurs à l'art de la musique et de la chanson

claims.statement: In popular belief, an artist (artiste) is thought to be possessed by this divinity while performing.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan populer, seniman (artiste) dianggap dirasuki sosok ilahi ini saat tampil.
claims.quote: Dans les idées de la croyance populaire, l'artiste lui est assimilé parce qu'il serait possédé par cette divinité pendant ses prestations artistique

claims.statement: The Azizás are a beneficent supernatural race in Fon mythology (mitologia fon).
claims.statement_id: Azizá (Azizás) adalah bangsa gaib yang baik hati dalam mitologi Fon (mitologia fon).
claims.quote: Os Azizás são uma raça sobrenatural benéfica na mitologia fon.

claims.statement: They are described as small, hairy people (pequenas e cabeludas) who live in anthills and silk-cotton trees.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai orang kecil berambut lebat (pequenas e cabeludas) yang tinggal di sarang semut dan pohon kapuk.
claims.quote: São descritos como pessoas pequenas e cabeludas que vivem em formigueiros e mafumeiras.

claims.statement: The Jeje oral tradition (tradição oral Jeje) has a single divinity named Azizá.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi lisan Jeje (tradição oral Jeje) mengenal satu sosok ilahi tunggal bernama Azizá.
claims.quote: Por exemplo, a tradição oral Jeje tem uma divindade chamada

claims.statement: Among the Urhobo he is described as a big man (homem grande) with one arm and one leg, dressed in white.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Urhobo, ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki besar (homem grande) berlengan satu dan berkaki satu yang berpakaian putih.
claims.quote: Descrito como um homem grande com um só braço e uma só perna, vestindo branco.

claims.statement: In one quarter Aziza was believed to be a one-handed and one-legged god.
claims.statement_id: Di satu kalangan, Aziza dipercaya sebagai dewa bertangan satu dan berkaki satu (one handed and one legged god).
claims.quote: In one quarter, it was believed that Aziza is a one handed and a one legged god

claims.statement: He does both good and bad: badly to bad people and good to good people.
claims.statement_id: Ia berbuat baik dan buruk: berbuat buruk kepada orang jahat dan baik kepada orang baik (good to good people).
claims.quote: He does what is good and what is bad. He does badly to bad people and good to good people.

claims.statement: Aziza is the herald of dawn, lord of the brief passage between night and dawn.
claims.statement_id: Aziza adalah pembawa kabar fajar (herald of dawn), penguasa saat peralihan singkat antara malam dan fajar.
claims.quote: Aziza is the herald of dawn, lord of the fleetingly transient state between night and dawn

claims.statement: Aziza is addressed as the king of the forest as well as of the earth.
claims.statement_id: Aziza disapa sebagai raja hutan sekaligus raja bumi (king of the forest as well as of the earth).
claims.quote: peculiar aspect of its potent power is acknowledged in Urhobo folklores where Aziza is addressed as the ... king of the forest as well as of the earth

claims.statement: Hunters cover the place with cabald or snuff, enough to drive Aziza far from its abode.
claims.statement_id: Para pemburu menaburkan cabald atau tembakau sedotan (snuff) untuk mengusir Aziza jauh dari tempatnya.
claims.quote: they cover the entire place with cabald or snuff which is enough to drive Aziza far away from its abode.

claims.statement: The dingonek is a creature said to have been seen near Lake Victoria in 1907 by hunter John Alfred Jordan and his party, as recounted by Edgar Beecher Bronson in his 1910 memoir In Closed Territory.
claims.statement_id: Dingonek adalah makhluk yang konon terlihat dekat Danau Victoria (Lake Victoria) pada 1907 oleh pemburu John Alfred Jordan dan rombongannya, sebagaimana dikisahkan Edgar Beecher Bronson dalam memoar tahun 1910, In Closed Territory.
claims.quote: The dingonek is a creature said to have been seen near Lake Victoria in 1907 by big game hunter John Alfred Jordan and members of his hunting party, as recounted by fellow big-game hunter Edgar Beecher Bronson in his 1910 memoir In Closed Territory.

claims.statement: This account was followed by a 1913 article by Charles William Hobley in the East Africa Natural History Society, claiming further accounts of similarly described creatures.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu disusul artikel Charles William Hobley tahun 1913 di East Africa Natural History Society, yang mengaku menemukan laporan lain tentang makhluk serupa.
claims.quote: This account was followed by an article published in 1913 in the East Africa Natural History Society by Charles William Hobley, in which he claims to have encountered further accounts of similarly described creatures.

claims.statement: In 1918 an article in MacLean's declared the beast a newly discovered animal species.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1918, sebuah artikel di MacLean's menyatakan makhluk itu spesies hewan (animal species) yang baru ditemukan.
claims.quote: In 1918, an article published by MacLean's declared that the beast was a newly discovered animal species.

claims.statement: One member of the party, Mataia, claims to have seen it twice, yet Bronson expressed skepticism.
claims.statement_id: Seorang anggota rombongan, Mataia, mengaku melihatnya dua kali, tetapi Bronson meragukannya (skepticism).
claims.quote: One member of the party, Mataia, claims to have seen it twice, yet Bronson expressed skepticism.

claims.statement: The witness quoted by Hobley describes it as spotted like a leopard, covered with scales and with a head like an otter; he did not see the long fangs described by Jordan.
claims.statement_id: Saksi yang dikutip Hobley menggambarkannya bertotol seperti macan tutul (leopard), bersisik, berkepala seperti berang-berang (otter), dan tidak melihat taring panjang seperti yang diceritakan Jordan.
claims.quote: He describes it as spotted like a leopard, covered with scales, and having a head like an otter; he did not see the long fangs described by Mr. Jordan.

claims.statement: The beast came floating down the river on a big log, and the witness estimated its length at about sixteen feet.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu hanyut di sungai di atas batang kayu besar (big log), dan saksi memperkirakan panjangnya sekitar enam belas kaki (sixteen feet).
claims.quote: The beast came floating down the river on a big log, and he estimated its length at about sixteen feet

claims.statement: According to Jordan it lives in Lake Victoria Nyanza and its numerous tributaries, with no record of it seen anywhere else in the world.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Jordan, makhluk itu hidup di Danau Victoria Nyanza dan banyak anak sungainya (tributaries), dan tidak pernah tercatat terlihat di tempat lain.
claims.quote: It lives in Lake Victoria Nyanza and its numerous tributaries, and there is no record of the monster having been seen in any other part of the world.

claims.statement: Jordan says the lake creature was christened Dingonek by the Lumbwa, and reckons it would fetch five or ten thousand quid at least.
claims.statement_id: Jordan menyebut makhluk dari danau itu dinamai Dingonek oleh orang Lumbwa, dan memperkirakan nilainya lima sampai sepuluh ribu pound (five or ten thousand quid).
claims.quote: comes up the Maggori River out of the lake the Lumbwa have christened Dingonek.

claims.statement: The Lumbwa described it as some sort of cross between a sea serpent, a leopard and a whale.
claims.statement_id: Orang Lumbwa melukiskannya sebagai semacam campuran ular laut (sea serpent), macan tutul (leopard), dan paus (whale).
claims.quote: some sort of cross between a sea serpent, a leopard, and a whale

claims.statement: Jordan describes it as fourteen or fifteen feet long, with a head as big as a lioness's but marked like a leopard, two long white fangs from the upper jaw, a back as broad as a hippo, scaled like an armadillo, and a broad fin tail.
claims.statement_id: Jordan menggambarkannya sepanjang empat belas atau lima belas kaki (fourteen or fifteen feet), berkepala sebesar singa betina bercorak macan tutul, bertaring putih panjang dari rahang atas, berpunggung selebar kuda nil (hippo), bersisik seperti armadillo, dan berekor sirip lebar.
claims.quote: fourteen or fifteen feet long, head big as that of a lioness but shaped and marked like a leopard, two long white fangs sticking down straight out of his upper jaw, back broad as a hippo, scaled like an armadillo, but colored and marked like a leopard, and a broad fin tail

claims.statement: Jordan says its fangs looked long enough to go clean through a man.
claims.statement_id: Jordan berkata taringnya tampak cukup panjang untuk menembus tubuh manusia (go clean through a man).
claims.quote: Blast that blighter's fangs, but they looked long enough to go clean through a man.

claims.statement: Jordan shot it with a .303 from less than ten yards, but though they watched waters and shores over several miles for two days, they saw neither it nor its tracks.
claims.statement_id: Jordan menembaknya dengan peluru .303 dari jarak kurang dari sepuluh yard (ten yards), tetapi meski mencari selama dua hari sepanjang beberapa mil, mereka tak melihatnya lagi atau jejaknya.
claims.quote: a .303, where placed, should have killed anything, for he was less than ten yards from me when I shot, but though we watched waters and shores over a range of several miles for two days, no sight did we get of him or his tracks.

claims.statement: According to information in the memoir, a great water serpent or reptile was seen near the north shore of the lake and worshipped by the natives, who took its coming as a harbinger of heavy crops and increasing herds.
claims.statement_id: Menurut keterangan dalam memoar itu, seekor ular atau reptil air besar (water serpent or reptile) kadang terlihat di pantai utara danau dan disembah penduduk, yang menganggap kedatangannya pertanda panen melimpah dan ternak bertambah.
claims.quote: a great water serpent or reptile was seen on or near the north shore of the lake, which was worshipped by the natives, who believed its coming a harbinger of heavy crops and large increase of their flocks and herds.

claims.statement: People of the north shore of the lake sacrificed burnt offerings of cattle and sheep to a huge, terrible lake reptile they called Luquata.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk pantai utara danau mempersembahkan korban bakaran sapi dan domba (cattle and sheep) kepada reptil danau raksasa berpenampilan mengerikan yang mereka sebut Luquata.
claims.quote: sacrificed burnt offerings of cattle and sheep to a lake reptile of great size and terrible appearance they called Luquata, which occasionally appeared along or near the shore

claims.statement: A jengu is a water spirit in the traditional beliefs of the Sawabantu groups of Cameroon, such as the Duala, Bakweri, Malimba, Subu, Bakoko and Oroko.
claims.statement_id: Jengu adalah roh air (water spirit) dalam kepercayaan tradisional kelompok Sawabantu di Kamerun, seperti Duala, Bakweri, Malimba, Subu, Bakoko, dan Oroko.
claims.quote: is a water spirit in the traditional beliefs of the Sawabantu groups of Cameroon, like the Duala, Bakweri, Malimba, Subu, Bakoko, and Oroko people.

claims.statement: Described as mermaid-like spirits, they live in rivers and the sea, bring good fortune to their worshippers, can cure disease and mediate with the spirit world.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai roh mirip putri duyung (mermaid-like) yang tinggal di sungai dan laut, membawa keberuntungan bagi pemujanya, dapat menyembuhkan penyakit, dan menjadi perantara dengan dunia roh.
claims.quote: Described as mermaid-like spirits, they live in rivers and the sea, bringing good fortune to those who worship them. They can also cure disease and act as intermediaries between worshippers and the world of spirits.

claims.statement: Descriptions of miengu vary by group, but they are usually beautiful, mermaid-like beings with long hair and lovely gap-teeth.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran miengu berbeda menurut suku, tetapi umumnya mereka makhluk cantik mirip putri duyung, berambut panjang, dan bergigi renggang yang indah (gap-teeth).
claims.quote: The description of miengu varies by ethnic group, but they are typically said to be beautiful, mermaid-like beings with long hair and beautiful gap-teeth.

claims.statement: Like a simbi in Kongo religion, a jengu is seen as a guardian of the natural world.
claims.statement_id: Seperti simbi dalam agama Kongo, jengu dipandang sebagai penjaga alam (guardian of the natural world).
claims.quote: Similar to a simbi in Kongo religion, a jengu is seen as a guardian of the natural world

claims.statement: The specialist later returns with a prophetic message from the miengu about the coming year.
claims.statement_id: Sang ahli ritual kemudian kembali membawa pesan bernubuat (prophetic message) dari miengu tentang tahun mendatang.
claims.quote: The specialist later returns with a prophetic message from the miengu about the upcoming year.

claims.statement: Observations by European traders and explorers show jengu worship was well established by the early 19th century, and early missionaries largely failed to suppress it.
claims.statement_id: Catatan pedagang dan penjelajah Eropa menunjukkan pemujaan jengu sudah mapan pada awal abad ke-19 (19th century), dan para misionaris awal gagal menekannya.
claims.quote: Observations by European traders and explorers prove that jengu-worship was well established by the early 19th century. Early missionaries largely failed in their attempts to suppress it.

claims.statement: The most prominent miengu ceremony today is the annual Ngondo celebration in Douala, first held in 1949.
claims.statement_id: Upacara miengu terpenting kini adalah perayaan Ngondo tahunan di Douala, yang pertama kali diadakan pada 1949.
claims.quote: The highest-profile miengu ceremony today is the annual Ngondo celebration in Douala, first held in 1949.

claims.statement: A cult member dives into the sea with the offering and later returns with a message from the miengu about the year ahead.
claims.statement_id: Seorang anggota kultus menyelam ke laut (dives into the sea) membawa persembahan, lalu kembali dengan pesan miengu tentang tahun yang akan datang.
claims.quote: One cult member dives into the sea with the gift and stays down as long as possible. Afterward, he returns with a message from the miengu about the year to come.

claims.statement: During initiation, cult members try to catch a crab, as this animal represents the liengu spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam inisiasi, anggota kultus berusaha menangkap seekor kepiting (crab), karena hewan ini melambangkan roh liengu.
claims.quote: Meanwhile, other cult members attempt to capture a crab from the waters, as this animal represents the liengu spirit.

claims.statement: The jengu spirit lives in rivers and the sea (rivas an sea).
claims.statement_id: Roh jengu tinggal di sungai dan laut (rivas an sea).
claims.quote: Jengu spirit dey live inside rivas an sea.

claims.statement: People describe the jengu as a mami wota spirit.
claims.statement_id: Orang menggambarkan jengu sebagai roh mami wota (mami wota spirit).
claims.quote: Pipo dey diskrib jengu as mami wota spirit.

claims.statement: They resemble Mami Wata figures, though belief in miengu probably predates most Mami Wata traditions.
claims.statement_id: Miengu mirip sosok Mami Wata, tetapi kepercayaan pada miengu kemungkinan lebih tua daripada kebanyakan tradisi Mami Wata (predates).
claims.quote: They are similar to West African Mami Wata figures, though belief in miengu likely predates most Mami Wata traditions.

claims.statement: In some traditions Jengu is a single god who replaces the miengu spirits or leads them; among the Isubu he is shown as a man with backwards feet.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian tradisi, Jengu adalah satu dewa (god) yang menggantikan golongan roh miengu atau memimpin mereka; di kalangan Isubu ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki berkaki terbalik (backwards feet).
claims.quote: In some traditions, this god replaces the class of miengu spirits, while in others, it acts as their leader. Among the Isubu, for example, this god is called Jengu, and is depicted as a man with backwards feet.

claims.statement: Bakweri belief speaks of a female deity named Mojili or Mojele.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan Bakweri mengenal dewi (female deity) bernama Mojili atau Mojele.
claims.quote: Bakweri belief talks of a female deity named Mojili or Mojele.

claims.statement: Moto won the right to stay in the village while Mojili had to flee to the sea; the Bakweri still worship Mojili as ruler of the maengu.
claims.statement_id: Moto memenangkan hak tinggal di desa, sedangkan Mojili terpaksa lari ke laut (sea); orang Bakweri masih memuja Mojili sebagai penguasa maengu.
claims.quote: Moto won the right to stay in the village, but Mojili was forced to flee to the sea. The Bakweri still worship Mojili as the ruler of the maengu.

claims.statement: Mojili became the ancestor of the maengu after losing a bet with Moto, ancestor of mankind, over who could make the longer-lasting fire.
claims.statement_id: Mojili menjadi leluhur maengu setelah kalah taruhan dengan Moto, leluhur umat manusia, tentang siapa yang bisa membuat api (fire) paling lama menyala.
claims.quote: Mojili became the progenitor of the maengu when she lost a bet with Moto, the ancestor of mankind, over who could build the longer-lasting fire.

claims.statement: The maengu are highly esteemed among the Wakweli and credited with superhuman powers.
claims.statement_id: Maengu sangat dihormati di kalangan Wakweli dan dianggap memiliki kekuatan adimanusia (superhuman powers).
claims.quote: The maengu are held in high esteem among the Wakweli and are credited with superhuman powers.

claims.statement: Achuhucanac is the rain god of Guanche religion on Tenerife, identified with the Supreme God (Achamán).
claims.statement_id: Achuhucanac adalah dewa hujan (rain god) dalam agama Guanche di Tenerife, yang disamakan dengan Dewa Tertinggi (Achamán).
claims.quote: Achuhucanac is the rain god in Guanche religion in Tenerife, identified with the Supreme God (Achamán).

claims.statement: Its name comes from the Guanche ašu_hu_kanak, meaning 'that is in the rain' or 'that who is in the rain'.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari bentuk Guanche ašu_hu_kanak yang berarti 'yang ada di dalam hujan' (that is in the rain).
claims.quote: Its name comes from: ašu_hu_kanak Guanche language that means "that is in the rain" or "that who is in the rain".

claims.statement: He belongs to the Guanche mythology of Tenerife (mythologie guanche de Tenerife).
claims.statement_id: Ia termasuk dalam mitologi Guanche di Tenerife (mythologie guanche de Tenerife).
claims.quote: dans la mythologie guanche de Tenerife

claims.statement: Achucanac and Acucanac are words recorded by Abreu Galindo and identified by Dr. Chil.
claims.statement_id: Achucanac dan Acucanac adalah kata-kata yang dicatat Abreu Galindo dan diidentifikasi oleh Dr. Chil (identified by Dr. Chil).
claims.quote: Achucanac and Acucanac are words given by Abreu Galindo, and identified by Dr. Chil, doubtless rightly,

claims.statement: They are identified with Achjucanac, translated as 'the sublime God'.
claims.statement_id: Kata-kata itu disamakan dengan Achjucanac, yang diterjemahkan sebagai 'Dewa yang Mulia' (the sublime God).
claims.quote: with Achjucanac,. translated ' the sublime God ' by

claims.statement: Espinosa gives Achuhucanac, which is plainly the same word as the Hucanech of Nunez de la Pena.
claims.statement_id: Espinosa mencatat bentuk Achuhucanac, yang jelas sama dengan Hucanech dari Nunez de la Pena (the same word).
claims.quote: Espinosa gives Achuhucanac. This is obviously the same word with the Hucanech of Nunez de la Pena, and

claims.statement: The peculiarity of the word is the syllable Hu between article and noun, clearly a preformative indicating greatness or holiness.
claims.statement_id: Kekhasan kata ini adalah suku kata Hu di antara kata sandang dan kata benda, yang jelas merupakan awalan yang menandakan keagungan atau kesucian (greatness or holiness).
claims.quote: The peculiarity of the present word is the syllable Hu fixed as a differentiation between the article and the noun. It is clearly a preformative indicating greatness or holiness.

claims.statement: Bunzi is a serpent water spirit and rain goddess of traditional Kongo religion, first venerated by the Woyo people of the Kingdom of Ngoyo.
claims.statement_id: Bunzi adalah roh air berwujud ular dan dewi hujan (goddess of rain) dalam agama tradisional Kongo, yang pertama kali dipuja orang Woyo di Kerajaan Ngoyo.
claims.quote: is a serpent water spirit and goddess of rain in traditional Kongo religion that was first venerated by the Woyo people of the Kingdom of Ngoyo.

claims.statement: Bunzi is sometimes shown as a multicoloured serpent who rewards her worshippers with an abundant harvest.
claims.statement_id: Bunzi kadang digambarkan sebagai ular beraneka warna (multicolored serpent) yang mengganjar pemujanya dengan panen melimpah.
claims.quote: Bunzi is sometimes depicted as a multicolored serpent that rewards those who worship her with an abundant harvest.

claims.statement: She is also said to appear in the rippling water of the river at sunset.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga konon tampak di riak air sungai saat matahari terbenam (at sunset).
claims.quote: She also said to appear in the rippling water of the river at sunset.

claims.statement: According to Kongo oral tradition, Bunzi is the daughter of Mboze, the Great Mother and wife of Kuitikuiti.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi lisan orang Kongo, Bunzi adalah putri Mboze, Ibu Agung (Great Mother) dan istri Kuitikuiti.
claims.quote: According to the oral tradition of the Kongo people, Bunzi is the daughter of Mboze, the Great Mother and wife of Kuitikuiti.

claims.statement: Bunzi was born as a baby serpent, and on seeing her Kuitikuiti knew Mboze had been unfaithful to him.
claims.statement_id: Bunzi lahir dalam wujud anak ular (baby serpent), dan ketika melihatnya Kuitikuiti tahu bahwa Mboze tidak setia kepadanya.
claims.quote: When Mboze gave birth, Bunzi was born in the form of a baby serpent. Upon seeing the child, Mboze's husband Kuitikuiti knew that she had been unfaithful to him.

claims.statement: Learning that Bunzi's father was their son Makanga, Kuitikuiti killed Mboze; Bunzi then took on her mother's rain-bringing power.
claims.statement_id: Setelah tahu ayah kandung Bunzi adalah putra mereka, Makanga, Kuitikuiti membunuh Mboze; Bunzi lalu mewarisi kekuatan ibunya mendatangkan hujan (rain-bringing power).
claims.quote: When he learned the biological father of Bunzi was their son Makanga, he killed Mboze for her transgression. Bunzi took on her mother's rain-bringing power.

claims.statement: According to legend, a rainbow appearing in the sky is Bunzi.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, pelangi (rainbow) yang muncul di langit adalah Bunzi.
claims.quote: According to legend, when a rainbow appears in the sky, that is Bunzi.

claims.statement: The Yombe of the Republic of the Congo call the spirit Phulu Bunzi, a male lord of the water who devised a pact between Nzazi and Mbumba for harmony between earth and sky.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yombe di Republik Kongo menyebutnya Phulu Bunzi dan menganggapnya penguasa air laki-laki (male lord of the water), yang membuat perjanjian antara Nzazi dan Mbumba demi keselarasan bumi dan langit.
claims.quote: The Yombe people of the Republic of the Congo refer to Bunzi as Phulu Bunzi and consider the spirit to be a male lord of the water. He is said to have devised a pact between Nzazi (the god of thunder) and Mbumba (the rainbow water serpent) to create harmony between the earth and the skies.

claims.statement: One day, while he was visiting Mbumba, his son died; Phulu Bunzi blamed Mbumba and cut his head off.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari, saat ia mengunjungi Mbumba, putranya meninggal; Phulu Bunzi menyalahkan Mbumba dan memenggal kepalanya (cut his head off).
claims.quote: One day while he was visiting Mbumba, his son died. Consequently, Phulu Bunzi blamed Mbumba and cut his head off.

claims.statement: Bunzi Mons, a mountain on Venus, is named after her.
claims.statement_id: Bunzi Mons, sebuah gunung di Venus (mountain on Venus), dinamai menurut namanya.
claims.quote: The Bunzi Mons, a mountain on Venus, is named after her.

claims.statement: In Ngoyo mythology (Congo), Bunzi is a rain goddess (deessa de la pluja) and the daughter of Mboze, the Great Mother.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Ngoyo (Congo), Bunzi adalah dewi hujan (deessa de la pluja) dan putri Mboze, Sang Ibu Agung.
claims.quote: a la mitologia Ngoyo (Congo) és una deessa de la pluja. És la filla d'Mboze, la Gran Mare.

claims.statement: Mboze took her own son Makanga as a lover and gave birth to Bunzi (va donar a llum a Bunzi).
claims.statement_id: Mboze menjadikan putranya sendiri, Makanga, sebagai kekasih dan melahirkan Bunzi (va donar a llum a Bunzi).
claims.quote: Mboze va prendre el seu propi fill, Makanga, com a amant i va donar a llum a Bunzi.

claims.statement: Bunzi assumed her mother's power over rain (poder de la pluja).
claims.statement_id: Bunzi mengambil alih kekuatan hujan (poder de la pluja) ibunya.
claims.quote: Bunzi va assumir el poder de la pluja de la seva mare.

claims.statement: Mbielu-mbielu-mbielu is a cryptid reportedly seen at the Likouala River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
claims.statement_id: Mbielu-mbielu-mbielu adalah kriptid (cryptid) yang konon terlihat di Sungai Likouala, Republik Demokratik Kongo.
claims.quote: is a cryptid reportedly seen at the Likouala River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

claims.statement: Its name means 'the animal with planks growing out of its back'.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti 'hewan dengan papan yang tumbuh dari punggungnya' (planks growing out of its back).
claims.quote: the animal with planks growing out of its back

claims.statement: Cryptozoologists never fully agreed on its appearance, but it is said to have green 'planks' on its back, leading some to propose it is a surviving stegosaurid.
claims.statement_id: Para kriptozoolog tidak pernah sepakat soal wujudnya, tetapi ia disebut memiliki 'papan' hijau di punggungnya sehingga sebagian mengusulkan ia stegosaurid (stegosaurid) yang masih hidup.
claims.quote: has never been completely agreed upon by cryptozoologists; however, it is said to have green ... growing out of its back, leading some in cryptozoological circles to propose that the alleged animal represents an extant stegosaurid.

claims.statement: It has also been compared with another purported cryptid, the nguma-monene.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dibandingkan dengan kriptid lain, nguma-monene.
claims.quote: Similarities have also been drawn to another purported cryptid from Africa, the nguma-monene.

claims.statement: It is said usually to lie submerged in water with only its back showing, often covered in green algae, and to be most active in the afternoon.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini konon biasanya terbenam di air (submerge itself in water) dengan hanya punggung yang tampak, sering tertutup ganggang hijau, dan paling aktif pada sore hari.
claims.quote: Mbielu-mbielu-mbielu is said to typically submerge itself in water with only its back showing, which is often covered in (usually green) algal growths. It has also been claimed that mbielu-mbielu-mbielu is mostly active in the afternoon.

claims.statement: It is said to be seen in the rivers and lakes of Likouala-Mossaka.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon dapat dilihat di sungai dan danau Likouala-Mossaka (rivers and lakes).
claims.quote: it has been said that mbielu-mbielu-mbielu can be sighted in the rivers and lakes of Likouala-Mossaka in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

claims.statement: Biologist Roy Mackal held the theory that it was a giant monitor lizard.
claims.statement_id: Ahli biologi Roy Mackal menganut teori bahwa makhluk ini biawak raksasa (giant monitor lizard).
claims.quote: American biologist Roy Mackal subscribed to the theory that mbielu-mbielu-mbielu was a giant monitor lizard; however, Mackal also regarded the animal as an

claims.statement: Anthropologist Dale A. Drinnon theorised it could be a giant crocodilian with a serrated back.
claims.statement_id: Antropolog Dale A. Drinnon berteori bahwa makhluk ini mungkin buaya raksasa (giant crocodilian) berpunggung bergerigi.
claims.quote: American anthropologist Dale A. Drinnon theorised that the creature could be a species of giant crocodilian with a serrated back.

claims.statement: In 1980 Odette Gesonget, a local from Bouanila in the Republic of the Congo, picked a Stegosaurus picture from Mackal's books to describe the creature.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1980, Odette Gesonget, warga Bouanila di Republik Kongo, memilih gambar Stegosaurus (Stegosaurus) dari buku yang dibawa Mackal untuk menggambarkan makhluk ini.
claims.quote: In 1980, Odette Gesonget (a local from Bouanila, the Republic of the Congo) selected an image of a Stegosaurus from books provided by Mackal in providing a description of mbielu-mbielu-mbielu.

claims.statement: She admitted she had never seen the creature herself and based her choice on what her parents and grandparents told her.
claims.statement_id: Namun ia mengaku tak pernah melihat makhluk itu sendiri dan memilih berdasarkan cerita orang tua dan kakek-neneknya (parents and grandparents).
claims.quote: However, she also disclosed that she had never actually witnessed the creature herself, having ostensibly based her selection on information shared by her parents and grandparents.

claims.statement: The second article calls it a mysterious creature (神秘生物) of Likouala in the Republic of the Congo (刚果共和国), usually living in water and resembling a giant crocodile (巨大的鳄鱼) with a serrated back.
claims.statement_id: Artikel kedua menyebutnya makhluk misterius (神秘生物) di Likouala, Republik Kongo (刚果共和国), yang biasanya hidup di air dan mirip buaya raksasa (巨大的鳄鱼) berpunggung bergerigi.
claims.quote: 是一种生存于刚果共和国利夸拉的神秘生物。Mbielu-Mbielu-Mbielu通常生活在水中，类似一个巨大的鳄鱼，但背上长有锯齿状

claims.statement: So far the only information on Mbielu-Mbielu-Mbielu is a few local sighting reports recorded by Roy Mackal (罗伊·麦考尔).
claims.statement_id: Informasi tentang Mbielu-Mbielu-Mbielu sejauh ini hanya berupa sedikit laporan penampakan warga setempat yang dicatat Roy Mackal (罗伊·麦考尔).
claims.quote: 目前关于Mbielu-Mbielu-Mbielu的资料仅有美国生物学与神秘动物学家罗伊·麦考尔 ... 所记载的少量当地人的目击报告。

claims.statement: Nyami Nyami, also called the Zambezi River god or Zambezi snake spirit, is one of the most important deities (Gottheiten) of the Tonga, who live in Zambia (Sambia) and Zimbabwe (Simbabwe) on both sides of the Zambezi.
claims.statement_id: Nyami Nyami, juga disebut dewa Sungai Zambezi atau roh ular Zambezi, adalah salah satu dewa (Gottheiten) terpenting orang Tonga, yang tinggal di Sambia dan Simbabwe di kedua sisi Zambezi.
claims.quote: auch bezeichnet als Gott des Zambezi-Flusses oder Zambezi-Schlangengeist, ist eine der wichtigsten Gottheiten des Volkes der Tonga, welches mehrheitlich auf der Nordseite des Zambezi, in Sambia, aber auch auf der Südseite des Flusses in Simbabwe lebt.

claims.statement: Nyami Nyami is usually shown as a male figure who protects (beschützt) the Tonga and sustains them in hard times; his form is a snake (Schlange) with a fish's head.
claims.statement_id: Nyami Nyami biasanya digambarkan sebagai sosok laki-laki yang melindungi (beschützt) orang Tonga dan menopang mereka di masa sulit; wujudnya ular (Schlange) berkepala ikan.
claims.quote: Nyami Nyami wird gewöhnlich als männliche Figur dargestellt, die das Volk der Tonga beschützt und ihm Halt in schwierigen Zeiten gibt. Seine äußere Form ist eine Schlange, die den Kopf eines Fisches besitzt.

claims.statement: He made sure there was enough water (Wasser) to irrigate the fields and enough fish (Fische) in the river.
claims.statement_id: Ia memastikan cukup air (Wasser) untuk mengairi ladang dan cukup ikan (Fische) di sungai.
claims.quote: Er sorgte dafür, dass genügend Wasser für die Bewässerung der Felder und genügend Fische im Fluss vorhanden waren.

claims.statement: The god and his wife (Gemahlin) lived in the underworld (Unterwelt) in the Kariba Gorge, and contact with them was made through the tribal elders.
claims.statement_id: Dewa ini dan istrinya (Gemahlin) tinggal di dunia bawah (Unterwelt) di Ngarai Kariba, dan hubungan dengan mereka dijalin lewat para tetua suku.
claims.quote: Eine Verbindung zum Gott und seiner Gemahlin, die beide in der Unterwelt in der Kariba-Schlucht wohnten, fand durch die Stammesältesten statt.

claims.statement: Today the Tonga hold that Nyami Nyami has withdrawn from the world of men (Welt der Menschen).
claims.statement_id: Kini orang Tonga berpendapat Nyami Nyami telah menarik diri dari dunia manusia (Welt der Menschen).
claims.quote: Heute sind die Tonga der Meinung, dass sich Nyami Nyami aus der Welt der Menschen zurückgezogen habe.

claims.statement: Pendants of the water god and walking sticks with snake-shaped, fish-headed knobs are now sold to tourists (Touristen) for cash.
claims.statement_id: Liontin dewa air ini dan tongkat jalan berkepala ular berkepala ikan kini dijual kepada wisatawan (Touristen) sebagai sumber uang tunai.
claims.quote: Darstellungen des Wassergottes als Anhänger, aus verschiedensten Materialien gearbeitet, und Spazierstöcke mit Knaufen in Schlangenform mit Fischkopf sind heute eine Möglichkeit, durch den Verkauf an Touristen etwas Bargeld einzunehmen zu können.

claims.statement: Nyami Nyami is the well-known name of the Tonga river god, believed to live in the Zambezi river and the Kariba dam.
claims.statement_id: Nyami Nyami adalah nama terkenal bagi dewa sungai (river god) orang Tonga, yang diyakini tinggal di Sungai Zambezi dan Bendungan Kariba.
claims.quote: Nyami Nyami is a famous name given to the river god of the Tonga people; he is believed to be residing in the Zambezi river and the Kariba dam.

claims.statement: The Tonga believe Nyami Nyami was angered because the dam builders disturbed his home and separated him from his wife.
claims.statement_id: Orang Tonga percaya Nyami Nyami murka (angered) karena pembangun bendungan mengusik tempat tinggalnya dan memisahkannya dari istrinya.
claims.quote: During the construction of the dam the Tonga people believe that nyami nyami was angered by the constructors who not only disturbed his residence but separated him from his wife when they divided the waters to construct a dam.

claims.statement: During construction of the Kariba dam in the 1960s, a group of workers drowned in the Zambezi River and their bodies could not be recovered for days.
claims.statement_id: Saat pembangunan Bendungan Kariba pada 1960-an (1960s), sekelompok pekerja tenggelam di Sungai Zambezi dan jasad mereka tak dapat ditemukan selama beberapa hari.
claims.quote: During the construction of the Kariba dam in 1960s a group of white men who were involved in the construction drowned in the Zambezi River and their bodies could not be retrieved for a number of days.

claims.statement: Some village headmen said the river god Nyami Nyami was behind their disappearance.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kepala desa menyatakan dewa sungai Nyami Nyami berada di balik hilangnya mereka (behind their disappearance).
claims.quote: Some of the village headmen stated that nyami nyami the river god was behind their disappearance.

claims.statement: The locals said this could only be resolved by a ritual of slaughtering a white goat and letting it float on the Zambezi River.
claims.statement_id: Warga menyatakan masalah itu hanya dapat diselesaikan dengan ritual menyembelih kambing putih (white goat) dan menghanyutkannya di Sungai Zambezi.
claims.quote: The local people assured the investors that this could only be resolved through a ritual that involved slaughtering a white goat and let it float in the Zambezi River.

claims.statement: The next day the drowned men's bodies were found floating and the goat's body had disappeared.
claims.statement_id: Keesokan harinya jasad para korban ditemukan mengapung dan bangkai kambing itu lenyap (goat had disappeared).
claims.quote: The following day the bodies of the drowned men were found floating on the river and the body of the goat had disappeared.

claims.statement: Nyami Nyami, the snake of the Zambezi river, is seen as the river god respected by the community.
claims.statement_id: Nyami Nyami, ular di Sungai Zambezi, dipandang sebagai dewa sungai (river god) yang dihormati masyarakat.
claims.quote: Nyami nyami the snake on the Zambezi river is seen as the river god respected by the community.

claims.statement: Nyami Nyami is seen as the god of the river in charge of the waters of the Zambezi.
claims.statement_id: Nyami Nyami dipandang sebagai dewa sungai yang menguasai perairan (in charge of the waters) Sungai Zambezi.
claims.quote: The nyami nyami on the other hand is seen as the god of the river in charge of the waters of the Zambezi river.

claims.statement: When resettled, the Tonga did not want to leave their ancestors' graves and wished to stay close to Nyami Nyami, their god of the river Zambezi.
claims.statement_id: Saat dipindahkan, orang Tonga enggan meninggalkan makam leluhur dan ingin tetap dekat dengan Nyami Nyami, dewa Sungai Zambezi mereka (god of the river Zambezi).
claims.quote: they also did not want to leave the graves of their ancestors and finally they wanted to be close to nyami nyami their famous god of the river Zambezi

claims.statement: The author argues that a chief's claim that the Kariba dam's crack is due to Nyami Nyami's anger should not be taken lightly.
claims.statement_id: Penulis menilai pernyataan seorang kepala adat bahwa retakan Bendungan Kariba disebabkan kemarahan Nyami Nyami tidak boleh dianggap remeh (crack).
claims.quote: The comment made by the chief that nyami nyami is angry that is why the Kariba dam has a crack should not be taken lightly.

claims.statement: According to the Kariba legend, in 1957 the Nyami Nyami struck: the worst floods on the Zambezi swept away much of the half-built dam and machinery, killing many workers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda Kariba, pada 1957 Nyami Nyami menyerang: banjir terburuk di Zambezi menghanyutkan sebagian bendungan dan alat berat serta menewaskan banyak pekerja (killing many of the workers).
claims.quote: In 1957, when the dam was well on its way to completion, the Nyami Nyami struck. The worst floods ever known on the Zambezi washed away much of the partly built dam and the heavy equipment, killing many of the workers.
